* Scenarios show that a client logged in as a space's anonymous account cannot set `dg_account` on an unowned account, by insert or update, and cannot change `agent_type`, `platform` or `account_local_id`. They fail before the change and pass after it.
* Scenarios show that a client cannot add a `LocalAccess` row for a space where it lacks editor access, whether it edits the account's space or owns the account. They fail before the change and pass after it.
* Scenarios show that such a client also cannot move a `LocalAccess` row into that space or delete one from it. These already pass before the change: through the API, the select policy hides those rows from a filtered write, and `safeupdate` rejects an unfiltered one. The space check is added to the update and delete policies anyway, so they don't depend on either.
* Scenarios show that what must keep working still works: space creation, `upsert_account_in_space` for an editor, an account owner renaming their account, and an editor renaming an unowned author account of their space.

## Out of Scope

* A claim function or claim table. Nothing sets `dg_account` as `authenticated` today; the DG accounts spec decides the claim mechanism.
* Dropping the unused `write_permission` column.
* Adding one's own account to another space. That waits for claim infrastructure, gated on an attested `LocalAccess` row.
* Checking that a `LocalAccess` row's account and space share a platform. After this change, someone who edits spaces on two platforms can still tie an unowned account of one to the other by a direct insert. No client writes `LocalAccess` directly.
* Rewriting the account policies to run once per query (<issue id="c2814438-ab26-4232-81f1-54c69dfa8cba" label="ENG-2446" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account" />).

## Notes

* Decisions and evidence: Roam [vtxvgZEKp](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/vtxvgZEKp>) (claiming) and [wB_q939-M](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/wB_q939-M>) (`LocalAccess` space check), each with a "Decided October 30" block.
* Space creation and group creation write as `service_role`, and `upsert_account_in_space` is `SECURITY DEFINER` and never sets `dg_account`, so the grants don't affect them.
* Blocks [ENG-2446](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account>). Related to [ENG-2439](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2439/require-editor-access-to-a-space-before-adding-accounts-to-it>), which also tightens `upsert_account_in_space`. Keep the branch local. It is stacked on <issue id="c187a719-3f2e-45e5-9088-1d61d65601e8" label="ENG-2443" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2443/check-rls-access-once-per-query-instead-of-once-per-row" />: it revokes no function `EXECUTE`, so it does not need the upgraded stack from `eng-2431-update-supabase-globally`.
* Before applying in production, look for claims and forged rows: accounts with a `dg_account` that are not `anonymous` (only space accounts should have one), and `LocalAccess` rows whose account has no other tie to that space's editors.

{"comments":[{"id":"6670783a-c183-4b18-8539-42f53b21f76e","body":"Implementation findings from rebasing this work on ENG-2446, which replace parts of the Solution's function lists. The goal and the `Done When` criteria don't change.

* **Functions that no longer exist.** ENG-2443 and ENG-2446 drop `can_view_specific_resource`, `is_my_account`, `account_in_shared_space`, `unowned_account_in_shared_space` and `can_access_account`. They are gone from the grants and revokes. The migration now runs after both, dated `20261030180000`.
* **`in_space` is revoked from `anon` instead of granted.** It was listed because the `Space` select policy called it. ENG-2443 moved that policy to `my_space_ids`. Now only write paths reach `in_space` as the caller, through `concept_in_space` and `content_in_space`. `anon`'s reads of `Space`, `my_spaces`, `my_concepts` and `file_access` work with the revoke.
* **New: `anon` keeps only `SELECT` on `concept_contributors` and `content_contributors`.** This follows the same reasoning as `sync_info`: the write policies on those tables call `in_space`, so `anon` should not hold write privileges there. No client writes to them as `anon`. `SELECT` stays because ENG-1837 relies on it for public nodes.
* **Table grants stay with ENG-1837.** `anon` still can't read `Concept`, `Content` or `Document`. In a rolled-back test, granting `SELECT` on those tables and on `ResourceAccess` returned 0 rows to `anon`, and all four grants were needed. ENG-1837's draft PR already adds them.
* **Tests.** `features/functionGrants.feature` also checks `in_space`, the new helpers `my_platform_account_ids` and `account_ids_in_shared_spaces`, `my_space_ids`, and refused inserts on both contributor tables. The insert check fails when `anon`'s write grant is put back.
* **`security_model.md`.** The doc describes only what is on this branch, with roadmap text trimmed. ENG-2438, ENG-2439 and ENG-2441 update it when they land.

Evidence so far: after `supabase db reset` from the migrations, the full cucumber suite passes (80 scenarios, 891 steps). `anon` can execute the same 34 function names that the schema files grant it, and no function keeps `PUBLIC` EXECUTE. This compares by name against a migration-built database. A database built from the schema files has not been compared yet, and the live checks in `Done When` have not been rerun.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-11-04T03:16:21.463Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-04T03:29:02.557Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"c220df10-bf52-40cf-b592-54f1405b4ef9","body":"Finding: the database cucumber suite cannot cover the flows behind this ticket's live checks. It reaches the database only through RPCs and table calls, so storage, sync tasks, the `create-space` edge function and schema updates are verified by hand. Moving them into cucumber is out of scope here and is captured as an issue candidate: [Cover storage, sync tasks, space creation and schema updates in the database cucumber suite](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kr33IACmG).","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-10-30T03:42:51.556Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-30T03:42:51.543Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null}],"hasNextPage":false}

{"comments":[{"id":"043de570-2586-4fda-a811-a058fb72c471","body":"This ticket's goal is smaller than its description says, and its fix should reach further. Hiding user ids (`auth.users.id`) from everywhere isn't practical ([accounts spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/s86_P-XTI)), so the plan is to make a known user id harmless instead (ENG-2456). This ticket now has one job: a user id shouldn't show which platform accounts belong to one person.

**Why that needs more than the view**

`PlatformAccount.dg_account` is the user id of an account's owner. Today it's set only on each space's login account (`agent_type = 'anonymous'`). Under Discourse Graph accounts, it will also be set on a person account when someone claims it.

Removing `dg_account` from `my_accounts` isn't enough, because the `PlatformAccount` table shows the same column to anyone with `partial` access to a space that uses the account. Once claims exist, this table would show:

* Which person owns each visible account. A person's user id will be visible in `group_membership` to the other members of their groups.
* Which accounts in different spaces belong to the same person, for a client that can see those spaces.

**Production on November 4, 2026**

| `agent_type` | Has `dg_account` | Has `LocalAccess` | Has `metadata` | Count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `person` | No | No | No | 3 |
| `person` | No | Yes | No | 537 |
| `anonymous` | Yes | No | No | 151 |

* Nothing leaks through these columns today. Peers can see the 537 person accounts, but `dg_account` is empty on all of them.
* Peers can't see the login accounts through `my_accounts` or `PlatformAccount`, because those accounts have no `LocalAccess` row. The ticket's Problem section is wrong to name their user ids as exposed there.

**Scope beyond Done When**

* Replace the `SELECT` grant on `PlatformAccount` for `authenticated` with a column list: `id`, `name`, `platform`, `account_local_id`, `write_permission`, `active`, `agent_type`.
* Revoke `UPDATE` on `metadata` from `authenticated`. No client code writes it, every production row is empty, and a column that clients can write but not read makes no sense. A later ticket can grant both when something uses it.
* Change the code that this breaks:
  * `getSessionUserData` in `apps/website/app/utils/supabase/account.ts` filters on `dg_account` for a person session. No production person account has a `dg_account` yet.
  * Four website integration test files read their own `dg_account` as a space login.
  * The cucumber step "a user logged in space ... should see ... in the database" uses `select("*")`, which fails on `PlatformAccount`.
* Check for direct embeds of `PlatformAccount`, and for a bare `.select()` after a write. Both fail if they request a hidden column.

Proposed checks:

* A space peer can't read `dg_account` or `metadata` from `PlatformAccount`, and can't filter on them.
* A space peer still reads the listed columns.
* Row visibility and updates of `name` and `active` don't change.

**Required now?**

Not for today's data. It must land before the first claim, and it's cheapest now, while no client depends on these columns. A new `PlatformAccount` column, such as a claim's attestation level, also stays hidden until someone grants it.

**Anyone consulted?**

No one yet.

**Decision**

Include it in this ticket, unless a reviewer objects.

**Corrections to the current Solution**

* The migration must grant `EXECUTE` on `author_of_content` and `author_of_concept` to `anon` again. After ENG-2442, recreated functions no longer get that grant by default.
* The migration must sort after ENG-2442's migration. The commit on the branch still uses `20261008120000`.
* The branch is now `eng-2441-stop-my_accounts-from-exposing-auth-uids-and-metadata-to`.

**Evidence**

I tested the column list on a local database in a rolled-back transaction, as a space login, with two accounts. Reads of the listed columns, row visibility and updates by `id` worked. `select *`, reads of `dg_account` and filters on `dg_account` or `metadata` were denied. I didn't test through PostgREST or test the `metadata` revoke. The cucumber scenarios will cover this.

**Rules for later work**

* ENG-2444: `my_pseudo_accounts` returns `dg_account`, so it must stay a definer view.
* ENG-1837 and ENG-2444: any `anon` grant on `PlatformAccount` must use the same column list.
* ENG-2445: plugin reads of the table must name their columns.
* Discourse Graph accounts: column grants apply to all rows, so a person can't read their own claim from the table. Claim status needs a function or a view.

**Not covered**

* User ids stay readable in `SpaceAccess`, `ResourceAccess`, `group_membership` and `my_pseudo_accounts`. The [accounts spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/s86_P-XTI) explains why, with the pros and cons of hiding them.
* `AgentIdentifier.value` is readable from `reader` access. Where it holds an email, that email can also link one person's accounts across spaces.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-11-04T18:06:52.622Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-04T18:06:52.536Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null}],"hasNextPage":false}

{"comments":[{"id":"9d9a9125-6ee0-4823-8572-50419b43e8da","body":"`accounts_in_my_partial_spaces` now has `security_barrier`. Without it, a caller's non-leakproof filter ran below the access join and saw account ids from other spaces. Timings don't change: a partial lookup is 0.05 ms with or without it. `my_accounts` has the same gap, and this change doesn't address it.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-11-02T14:49:09.808Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-02T14:49:09.782Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"6e6cb5fc-de11-40fb-a9ff-3b5ecc85b30f","body":"This corrects my previous comment after the delegated review. The timings and policy text there are out of date.

**Implementation findings:**

* `accounts_in_my_partial_spaces` now uses `DISTINCT`. Without it, the view returned one row per membership, so its row count revealed memberships that `LocalAccess` hides at partial level. No account ids were exposed beyond what the caller could already see. My previous comment missed this.
* The `PlatformAccount` select policy no longer has a separate reader branch. The view already covers partial and above, so the branch allowed nothing extra and built `my_space_ids` on every query.
* Old and new policies gave the same results in 1,324 probes across partial, reader and editor access, direct and through groups, with 0 differences. These probes were rerun on the final policies.

**Performance:** Median timings in ms at 20,020 accounts and 179 `SpaceAccess` rows, on generated data. Row counts match before and after.

| Query | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| All visible accounts | 826.04 | 9.81 |
| Lookup, own space | 0.10 | 0.05 |
| Lookup, partial space | 0.09 | 0.05 |
| Batch of 100 ids, partial space | 4.31 | 0.43 |
| Batch of 1,000 ids, partial space | 42.75 | 5.81 |
| Rename 100 accounts | 972.68 | 18.21 |
| Account upsert | 2.35 | 2.18 |

The single-row slowdown on `PlatformAccount` from my previous comment is gone. `AgentIdentifier` of one account is the one read still slightly slower, at 0.41 → 0.46 ms.

**`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, as a logged-in user:** one run each, same data. `PlatformAccount` select: 832.74 → 10.32 ms. Account upsert: 2.92 → 3.30 ms. The upsert doesn't go through these policies, and its medians above show no slowdown, so I read that difference as noise.

**Merge order with ENG-2442:** ENG-2442's migration runs a `REVOKE` on `unowned_account_in_shared_space`, which this migration drops. ENG-2442 needs to land first, or its migration needs updating.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-11-02T14:10:57.124Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-02T14:10:57.080Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"04d79259-bada-4416-a9b7-74123aee1728","body":"This replaces the approach and numbers in my previous comment. We no longer accept the partial-space regression.

**Implementation findings:**

* The partial branch of the `PlatformAccount` select policy now uses a one-column definer view, `accounts_in_my_partial_spaces`, not `account_ids_in_shared_spaces`. The planner can inline a view, so one account can be checked without building the whole set, and a full read still builds a hash once. The view returns only account ids the caller can already see, with no `space_id`. It's granted `SELECT` to `authenticated` and `service_role` only.
* `my_user_accounts` now has `ROWS 10`. Its default estimate of 1,000 rows made the planner scan `SpaceAccess`, and without the hint the view's full read took 92 ms at production's `SpaceAccess` size. The hint changes only the estimate, so it doesn't change what anyone can see. Resource-table reads did not get slower with it.
* `account_ids_in_shared_spaces` remains for `LocalAccess` and `AgentIdentifier` writes.

**Performance:** Single-row reads are still about 0.1 ms slower, so "neither is slower" doesn't hold strictly for them. Larger reads are faster. Median timings in ms at 20,020 accounts and 179 `SpaceAccess` rows (production has about 180), on generated data:

| Query | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| All visible accounts | 785.74 | 6.49 |
| Lookup, own space | 0.08 | 0.14 |
| Lookup, partial space | 0.08 | 0.18 |
| Rename 100 accounts | 918.00 | 11.97 |
| Account upsert | 2.09 | 2.08 |
| Batch of 100 ids, partial space | 4.01 | 1.11 |

**`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, as a logged-in user:** one run each, same data. `PlatformAccount` select: 808.13 → 8.91 ms. Account upsert: 2.92 → 3.00 ms, which is within noise (the upsert doesn't go through these policies).

Clients read authors through `my_accounts`, which doesn't use these policies, so this change doesn't affect those reads. Reading the table directly is now faster than `my_accounts` for batches of 100 or more, which supports moving those reads later.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-11-01T23:37:48.939Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-01T23:37:48.892Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"b27f3157-3767-4757-94e1-bcf069df9b93","body":"**Implementation finding:** Checks on readable spaces use a per-row `EXISTS` on `LocalAccess`, through its primary key, against a once-per-query list of the caller's spaces. With `account_ids_in_shared_spaces` alone, a single-account lookup took about 8 ms at 20,020 accounts, because the helper builds the full account set. `generic_entity_access` uses the same `LocalAccess` check, not the helper.

The helper remains for the partial branch of the `PlatformAccount` select, and for `LocalAccess` and `AgentIdentifier` writes. Inside a policy, `LocalAccess` is filtered by its own reader-level select policy, so an inline check can't see partial access. A `LocalAccess` policy that queried `LocalAccess` would also recurse.

**Performance gap:** "Neither is slower" doesn't hold for single-account lookups. Median timings in ms at 20,020 accounts, on generated data:

| Query | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| All visible accounts | 799.29 | 12.55 |
| Lookup, own space | 0.08 | 0.14 |
| Lookup, reader space | 0.10 | 0.14 |
| Lookup, partial space | 0.08 | 8.73 |
| Rename 100 accounts | 883.56 | 12.68 |
| Account upsert | 2.17 | 2.18 |

The partial-space lookup is the one real regression, and we accept it. It builds every account of the caller's partial spaces once per query, about 1 ms per 2,000 accounts. This number may change if we change which accounts partial access shows. We don't yet know in which direction: that check would depend on the caller's grants instead of the number of accounts, and we haven't measured it.

**`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, as a logged-in user:** One run each at 20,020 accounts, before and after on the same database, on battery power. Compare them with each other, not with the table above.

| Query | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `PlatformAccount` select | 1207.15 ms | 19.01 ms |
| Account upsert | 4.61 ms | 4.18 ms |

In the after plan, the select's subplans are hashed and each runs once (`loops=1`).","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-11-01T20:56:01.405Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-01T20:56:01.298Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"7ba905cd-44d8-4cd7-af65-54f7f107c4e8","body":"`access_token` moved to ENG-2448, which drops the table. These scenarios and helpers no longer cover it.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-10-31T02:41:26.500Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-31T02:41:26.420Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null}],"hasNextPage":false}

{"comments":[{"id":"9cffaf28-dfa1-4539-81f6-91547896b190","body":"Implementation finding: `INSERT` on `PlatformAccount` is revoked from `authenticated` outright, instead of being granted per column as the Solution describes. `platform_account_insert_policy` is dropped. The `Done When` criteria and the `UPDATE` grant don't change.

* Why: the column grant and the policy could not let any direct insert through. Clients can't set `dg_account`, so `dg_account = auth.uid()` is never true. The unowned branch needs a `LocalAccess` row for the new account, and that row can't exist before the account does.
* What keeps working: clients still create unowned accounts, including authors, through `upsert_accounts_in_space`, `upsert_account_in_space` and `create_account_in_space`. These functions are `SECURITY DEFINER`, never set `dg_account`, and also add the account to the space.
* Correction to the October 30 comment: a plain insert now fails on the missing `INSERT` privilege, not on the insert policy. The deletion of the Website route still stands.
* Test: `features/accountWriteAccess.feature` has a new scenario showing that a direct unowned insert is refused. That insert was already refused before this change, so the scenario guards against reopening it.
* ENG-2446 no longer rewrites this policy. The full cucumber suite passes on the ENG-2446 branch with this change.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-11-04T02:07:45.674Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-04T02:07:45.544Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"c10d6eec-f163-40df-ace8-76dcd962123f","body":"Implementation finding: the Website's `POST /api/supabase/platform-account` route is deleted instead of having `dg_account` removed from its validator.

* After the column grants, the route can never succeed. Its `getOrCreateEntity` upsert is `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET` on every column it sends, and Postgres requires `UPDATE` on each of them even when there is no conflict. `platform` and `account_local_id` are no longer granted, so every call fails with `permission denied for table PlatformAccount`.
* A plain insert fails too: a new account has no `LocalAccess` row, so the insert policy's only way through was `dg_account = auth.uid()`, which the grants close.
* Before this change the route could only create an account owned by the caller, which is the claim this ticket removes. Nothing in `apps` or `packages` calls it; Roam and Obsidian create accounts through `create_account_in_space` and `upsert_accounts_in_space`.
* Both failures were verified in `psql` on the local test database as a space login, in a rolled-back transaction. Found by the delegated review; agreed with the ticket author on October 30.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-10-30T20:45:36.434Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-30T20:45:36.421Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null}],"hasNextPage":false}

{"title":"Stop users from joining another user's space access through a group membership","description":"## Problem

* Any signed-in user can insert a `group_membership` row whose `group_id` is another user's ID. The access checks (`my_user_accounts()`, and so `in_space`) then give them that user's space access, up to editor.
* Cause: `group_membership_insert_policy` is `is_group_admin(group_id) OR NOT group_exists(group_id)`. The second clause was meant for creating a group, but it passes for any user ID that is not yet a group.
* A user with reader access to a space can read its editor's ID from `SpaceAccess`, so a reader can become an editor. The same clause also lets anyone take over a group after its last member leaves.
* Reproduced locally: under the current rule, a reader of space s1 joined s1's editor as a group and `in_space(s1, 'editor')` went from false to true.

## Solution

* Make the insert rule `is_group_admin(group_id)` only, and drop the then-unused `group_exists` function.
* Nothing needs the removed clause: `create-group` adds the first admin with the service role, and `accept_group_invitation` runs as a security definer.

## Done When

* A Cucumber scenario shows a reader of a space failing to join its editor's ID as a group, and failing to upsert documents to that space afterwards.
* A Cucumber scenario shows that nobody can join a group after its last member leaves.
* Both scenarios fail against the current rule and pass with the fix; the existing group scenarios (create, invite, ~~admin adds member~~) still pass.

## Out of Scope

* Hiding `SpaceAccess.account_uid` from readers. It stops being exploitable once the insert rule is fixed.

## Notes

* Issue candidate: [https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Wwm8OO2uF](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Wwm8OO2uF>)
* Implemented on local branch `security-group-membership-insert`, based on `eng-2431-update-supabase-globally`. It adds no `REVOKE`, so it does not wait on <issue id="ee8e1ecc-5162-44f6-940e-1a8414da037c" label="ENG-2437" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2437/upgrade-the-production-supabase-postgres-version" />.

{"title":"Require editor access to a space before adding accounts to it","description":"## Problem

* `upsert_account_in_space` is `SECURITY DEFINER` and checks no access. Any caller, including one not logged in, can rename an unowned `PlatformAccount` in any space, link it to the space through `LocalAccess`, and add email identifiers to it. `upsert_accounts_in_space` and `create_account_in_space` call it and share the problem.
* For an account with an owner, the function also adds a `SpaceAccess` row for that owner. Two bugs make that branch fail today. If they were fixed, a caller could give an account they own editor access to any space: `least(my_permissions_in_space(space_id_), 'editor')` returns `editor` when the caller has no access, because `LEAST` ignores NULL.
* That branch should not exist. `LocalAccess` says an account belongs to a space and grants nothing. People will get `SpaceAccess` through their Discourse Graphs account, after its planned verification, not by being listed as an author.

## Solution

* At the start of `upsert_account_in_space`, raise `insufficient_privilege` unless `in_space(space_id_, 'editor')`.
* Remove the `SpaceAccess` branch. The `space_editor` and `permissions` input fields, and `permissions_` of `create_account_in_space`, are then ignored; keep them so existing clients keep working.
* Revoke EXECUTE on the three functions from `PUBLIC` and `anon`. Plugins call them only after logging in.

## Done When

* Cucumber scenarios show that a client that is not logged in, a user with no access to the space, and a user with reader access all fail to add or rename accounts through it, and the account's name is unchanged.
* A Cucumber scenario shows an editor adding an account that has an owner, and the owner gains no access to the space.
* The existing callers still work: document, content and concept upserts (security invoker, editor-only insert rules) and Roam's `upsertUsers`. The full Cucumber suite passes.

## Out of Scope

* An editor of their own space can still rename any account on the same platform through the upsert's name update. This needs its own issue candidate.

## Notes

* Issue candidate: [https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/5cTXWhzAt](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/5cTXWhzAt>)
* Implemented on local branch `eng-2439-require-editor-access-to-a-space-before-adding-accounts-to`, based on `eng-2431-update-supabase-globally`.
* Blocked by [ENG-2437](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2437/upgrade-the-production-supabase-postgres-version>): on Supabase Postgres 17.6.1.106, calling a function the caller lacks EXECUTE on crashes the server, so the revokes must wait for the production upgrade.

{"title":"Stop my_accounts from exposing auth uids and metadata to space peers","description":"## Problem

* The `my_accounts` view returns `dg_account` (the Supabase auth uid) and `metadata` for every account in a space where the caller has at least `partial` access. The view is not `security_invoker`, so its own filter decides what peers see, not the row-level security on `PlatformAccount`.
* Auth uids are not secrets by design, but some checks treat knowing one as enough. <issue id="95a59c6b-c4e5-4759-8984-0530922c8f44" label="ENG-2438" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2438/stop-users-from-joining-another-users-space-access-through-a-group" /> is one: it needs only a uid to take over someone's access. A space's anonymous account holds `editor` on its space, so its uid is the most valuable target.
* No code reads `dg_account` or `metadata` from `my_accounts`. Code that needs `dg_account` reads it from `PlatformAccount` filtered on the caller's own uid, from `my_pseudo_accounts`, or through the service client.

## Solution

* Drop `dg_account` and `metadata` from `my_accounts`.
* `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` cannot remove columns, so the migration drops and recreates the view. `author_of_content` and `author_of_concept` return `SETOF public.my_accounts`, so they are dropped and recreated too.
* Recreating the view loses its grants, so the migration repeats the `REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE` for `anon` and `authenticated`.
* Regenerate `dbTypes` from a fresh database.

## Done When

* An authenticated user who shares a space with another account cannot read that account's `dg_account` or `metadata` through `my_accounts`.
* A user still reads their own accounts and their space peers' `id`, `name`, `platform`, `account_local_id`, `write_permission`, `active`, and `agent_type` through `my_accounts`.
* The author embeds in `packages/database/src/lib/queries.ts` and Obsidian's `fetchUserNames` work unchanged.
* `anon` and `authenticated` cannot write through `my_accounts`.

## Out of Scope

* The group-membership hole itself (<issue id="95a59c6b-c4e5-4759-8984-0530922c8f44" label="ENG-2438" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2438/stop-users-from-joining-another-users-space-access-through-a-group" />).
* Making `my_accounts` `security_invoker` or otherwise changing its row filter.

## Notes

* Source: Roam issue candidate `-SNrs-Lj_` (discourse-graphs graph). Found by reading the schema during a security review; not reproduced against a database.
* A fix exists on local branch `Restrict_my_accounts` (commit 1f123aa1e).

{"title":"Grant database functions only to the roles that call them","description":"## Problem

* `base.sql` sets default privileges that grant EXECUTE on every new function in `public` to `anon` (no login) and `authenticated` (logged in). Nobody chose these grants function by function. 25 of Supabase's 54 security-definer function warnings are grants that no client uses.
* An unused grant lets anyone call a `SECURITY DEFINER` function directly, outside the flow it was written for. The function runs with the owner's rights and skips row-level security. <issue id="1a223b96-4ee6-4f9f-ac40-ebc67c45c2a0" label="ENG-2439" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2439/require-editor-access-to-a-space-before-adding-accounts-to-it" /> shows what one direct call can do.
* Each new function is callable without a login unless someone remembers to revoke it. Public nodes will give `anon` real access for the first time, so the grants need to say which functions that opens.
* Four policies call `auth.uid()` once per row instead of once per query (Supabase's repeated-auth-check warnings).

## Solution

* Revoke EXECUTE from `anon` and `authenticated` on the functions that only triggers call: `after_delete_space`, `after_delete_update_fref`, `after_insert_fref`, `on_delete_local_reference`, `on_update_local_reference`, `on_delete_space_revoke_local_access`, and `is_last_local_reference` (called only by the two `local_reference` triggers; called directly, it reveals whether a row exists in a space the caller can't read).
* Revoke EXECUTE from `anon` only on functions that nothing calls without a login: `create_account_in_space`, `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space`, `file_exists`, `create_secret_token`, `accept_group_invitation`, `generic_entity_access`, `in_group`, `is_group_admin`, `group_exists`, `unowned_account_in_shared_space`. Revoke `anon`'s privileges on `sync_info` too.
* Change the default privileges in `base.sql` so new functions get no `anon` grant. Add an explicit `GRANT` to both roles for the nine functions `anon` reaches now or will reach for public nodes: `in_space`, `can_view_specific_resource`, `is_my_account`, `get_secret_token`, `my_user_accounts`, `my_space_ids`, `file_access`, `account_in_shared_space`, `can_access_account`.
* Write `(SELECT auth.uid())` instead of `auth.uid()` in the `group_membership` delete policy and the three `secret_token` policies.
* Next to each `GRANT` and `REVOKE`, add a `--` comment naming the client or policy that needs the grant.
* Add `packages/database/doc/security_model.md`, describing the grants after this change, the Supabase findings that remain and why, and the rules for new functions.

## Done When

* `anon` gets a permission error calling a revoked function (new cucumber scenario).
* Deleting content and file references still runs the triggers (new cucumber scenario). Postgres checks EXECUTE on a trigger function when the trigger is created, not when it fires.
* The full cucumber suite passes unchanged.
* Live checks, for flows cucumber does not reach (none fails with a permission error):
  * Roam and Obsidian publish a node with an image; Roam republishes it after the image changes; Roam imports a shared node with an image.
  * Roam sync runs to completion.
  * A fresh Roam graph or Obsidian vault connects, creating its space through the `create-space` edge function.
  * The website opens from a plugin's admin panel (`/auth/token` handoff, before login).
  * A group invitation created in a plugin's admin panel is accepted on the website.
  * A node type's definition is changed in Roam and synced.
* A database built from the schema files has the same function grants as one built from the migrations.
* The Supabase advisor no longer reports the 25 unused-grant warnings or the 4 repeated-auth-check warnings.

## Out of Scope

* The other 29 security-definer function warnings. `security_model.md` records why they remain.
* Changing the logic of any function or policy beyond the `auth.uid()` rewrite.

## Notes

* Source: Roam issue candidate `5CHcLj89v` (discourse-graphs graph). Evidence: Supabase security advisor snapshot of October 27, 2026; grants verified on the local test database with `has_function_privilege` and `pg_proc`.
* Callers were found by searching the schemas, edge functions, app and package sources, and cucumber features. Migrations were not searched.
* [ENG-2436](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2436/document-decisions-for-supabase-warnings>) records the decisions for the remaining Supabase warnings.
* Added during implementation:
  * EXECUTE revoked from `PUBLIC`, both in the `postgres` role's global function defaults (all schemas) and on existing non-extension functions in `public`. Every function granted EXECUTE to `PUBLIC`, so revoking `anon` alone changed nothing.
  * `concept_set_derived_columns` and `concept_propagate_derived_columns` (trigger functions that are not `SECURITY DEFINER`) revoked from `anon` and `authenticated`, following the rule for trigger functions.
  * `anon` revoked on `sync_info_id_seq` along with `sync_info`.
  * `anon` grants are explicit, including on the 38 functions that are not `SECURITY DEFINER`, so schema-built and migration-built databases match.

{"title":"Check account-table access once per query and drop the per-row account functions","description":"## Problem

* After <issue id="c187a719-3f2e-45e5-9088-1d61d65601e8" label="ENG-2443" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2443/check-rls-access-once-per-query-instead-of-once-per-row" />, the account tables are the last RLS policies that call `SECURITY DEFINER` functions once per row: `PlatformAccount`, the `LocalAccess` writes, `AgentIdentifier` and `access_token` call `account_in_shared_space`, `unowned_account_in_shared_space` and `is_my_account` with a row's account id.
* Postgres can't inline these functions, because they set `search_path`, so each call runs its own query for every row.
* The per-row functions also add to the number of similar access functions a reader has to tell apart.

## Solution

* Add two `SECURITY DEFINER` helpers that take no row column, so a policy can call them inside `(SELECT ...)` once per query:
  * `my_platform_account_ids()`: the `PlatformAccount` ids whose `dg_account` is the caller.
  * `account_ids_in_shared_spaces(level)`: the accounts with `LocalAccess` in a space where the caller has at least `level`, with whether each is unowned. It joins the caller's uid set directly, so the planned `self_to_*` sets replace one join here.
* Rewrite those policies as `account_id IN (SELECT ...)` over the helpers, keeping what they allow.
* Rewrite the `PlatformAccount` branch of `generic_entity_access` to use `account_ids_in_shared_spaces('editor')`.
* Drop `account_in_shared_space`, `unowned_account_in_shared_space` and `is_my_account`, which then have no callers, and regenerate `dbTypes.ts`.

## Done When

* Per-table visibility and write scenarios for `PlatformAccount`, `LocalAccess`, `AgentIdentifier` and `access_token` are written and pass before the policy change, and still pass after it.
* No policy or function calls the three dropped functions, and the generated types no longer list them.
* The new helpers keep working after <issue id="6f3792cc-2a0b-468c-b494-4c14962920d9" label="ENG-2442" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2442/grant-database-functions-only-to-the-roles-that-call-them" />: each has explicit `EXECUTE` grants for the roles that call the policies.
* `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` as a logged-in user, before and after, is recorded for a direct `PlatformAccount` select and an account upsert. Neither is slower after the change.

## Out of Scope

* Changing what the account policies allow. The `LocalAccess` space check and the claiming restrictions are separate fixes.
* `group_membership` and `sync_info` policies.
* The `self_to_*` uid sets from the accounts design.

## Notes

* Split from <issue id="c187a719-3f2e-45e5-9088-1d61d65601e8" label="ENG-2443" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2443/check-rls-access-once-per-query-instead-of-once-per-row" />, which covers the resource and space tables.
* Blocked by <issue id="c187a719-3f2e-45e5-9088-1d61d65601e8" label="ENG-2443" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2443/check-rls-access-once-per-query-instead-of-once-per-row" />. Schedule after the fixes for the `LocalAccess` space check (Roam wB_q939-M) and for claiming unowned accounts (Roam vtxvgZEKp), so the new scenarios assert the fixed behavior.

{"title":"Stop clients from claiming platform accounts or adding accounts to spaces they don't edit","description":"## Problem

* Any client with editor access to a space can claim the space's unowned platform accounts, including the space's anonymous account. The `PlatformAccount` write policies let it set `dg_account` to its own user, and then it owns the account: it can update and delete it.
* Any client can tie an account to a space it has no access to. The `LocalAccess` write policies check the account, never the row's `space_id`. An editor of a space can add that space's unowned accounts to any other space, and an account owner can add their own account to any space.
* Both should be fixed before the account policies are rewritten in <issue id="c2814438-ab26-4232-81f1-54c69dfa8cba" label="ENG-2446" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account" />, so its scenarios assert the fixed behavior. Once `LocalAccess` carries claims in the DG accounts work, a forged row would become a way to act for a space.

## Solution

* Replace the table-wide `INSERT` and `UPDATE` grants on `PlatformAccount` for `authenticated` with column grants:
  * `INSERT` leaves out `id`, `dg_account` and `write_permission`.
  * `UPDATE` covers only `name`, `active` and `metadata`. It leaves out `dg_account`, `agent_type`, `platform`, `account_local_id` and `write_permission`.
* Add `space_id = any((SELECT public.my_space_ids('editor'))::bigint [])` to the `LocalAccess` insert, update and delete policies, keeping their account condition.
* Remove `dg_account` from the validator of the Website's `POST /api/supabase/platform-account`.

## Done When

* Scenarios show that a client logged in as a space's anonymous account cannot set `dg_account` on an unowned account, by insert or update, and cannot change `agent_type`, `platform` or `account_local_id`. They fail before the change and pass after it.
* Scenarios show that a client cannot add a `LocalAccess` row for a space where it lacks editor access, whether it edits the account's space or owns the account. They fail before the change and pass after it.
* Scenarios show that such a client also cannot move a `LocalAccess` row into that space or delete one from it. These already pass before the change: through the API, the select policy hides those rows from a filtered write, and `safeupdate` rejects an unfiltered one. The space check is added to the update and delete policies anyway, so they don't depend on either.
* Scenarios show that what must keep working still works: space creation, `upsert_account_in_space` for an editor, an account owner renaming their account, and an editor renaming an unowned author account of their space.

## Out of Scope

* A claim function or claim table. Nothing sets `dg_account` as `authenticated` today; the DG accounts spec decides the claim mechanism.
* Dropping the unused `write_permission` column.
* Adding one's own account to another space. That waits for claim infrastructure, gated on an attested `LocalAccess` row.
* Checking that a `LocalAccess` row's account and space share a platform. After this change, someone who edits spaces on two platforms can still tie an unowned account of one to the other by a direct insert. No client writes `LocalAccess` directly.
* Rewriting the account policies to run once per query (<issue id="c2814438-ab26-4232-81f1-54c69dfa8cba" label="ENG-2446" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account" />).

## Notes

* Decisions and evidence: Roam [vtxvgZEKp](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/vtxvgZEKp>) (claiming) and [wB_q939-M](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/wB_q939-M>) (`LocalAccess` space check), each with a "Decided October 30" block.
* Space creation and group creation write as `service_role`, and `upsert_account_in_space` is `SECURITY DEFINER` and never sets `dg_account`, so the grants don't affect them.
* Blocks [ENG-2446](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account>). Related to [ENG-2439](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2439/require-editor-access-to-a-space-before-adding-accounts-to-it>), which also tightens `upsert_account_in_space`. Keep the branch local. It is stacked on <issue id="c187a719-3f2e-45e5-9088-1d61d65601e8" label="ENG-2443" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2443/check-rls-access-once-per-query-instead-of-once-per-row" />: it revokes no function `EXECUTE`, so it does not need the upgraded stack from `eng-2431-update-supabase-globally`.
* Before applying in production, look for claims and forged rows: accounts with a `dg_account` that are not `anonymous` (only space accounts should have one), and `LocalAccess` rows whose account has no other tie to that space's editors.

{"comments":[{"id":"043de570-2586-4fda-a811-a058fb72c471","body":"This ticket's goal is smaller than its description says, and its fix should reach further. Hiding user ids (`auth.users.id`) from everywhere isn't practical ([accounts spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/s86_P-XTI)), so the plan is to make a known user id harmless instead (ENG-2456). This ticket now has one job: a user id shouldn't show which platform accounts belong to one person.

**Why that needs more than the view**

`PlatformAccount.dg_account` is the user id of an account's owner. Today it's set only on each space's login account (`agent_type = 'anonymous'`). Under Discourse Graph accounts, it will also be set on a person account when someone claims it.

Removing `dg_account` from `my_accounts` isn't enough, because the `PlatformAccount` table shows the same column to anyone with `partial` access to a space that uses the account. Once claims exist, this table would show:

* Which person owns each visible account. A person's user id will be visible in `group_membership` to the other members of their groups.
* Which accounts in different spaces belong to the same person, for a client that can see those spaces.

**Production on November 4, 2026**

| `agent_type` | Has `dg_account` | Has `LocalAccess` | Has `metadata` | Count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `person` | No | No | No | 3 |
| `person` | No | Yes | No | 537 |
| `anonymous` | Yes | No | No | 151 |

* Nothing leaks through these columns today. Peers can see the 537 person accounts, but `dg_account` is empty on all of them.
* Peers can't see the login accounts through `my_accounts` or `PlatformAccount`, because those accounts have no `LocalAccess` row. The ticket's Problem section is wrong to name their user ids as exposed there.

**Scope beyond Done When**

* Replace the `SELECT` grant on `PlatformAccount` for `authenticated` with a column list: `id`, `name`, `platform`, `account_local_id`, `write_permission`, `active`, `agent_type`.
* Revoke `UPDATE` on `metadata` from `authenticated`. No client code writes it, every production row is empty, and a column that clients can write but not read makes no sense. A later ticket can grant both when something uses it.
* Change the code that this breaks:
  * `getSessionUserData` in `apps/website/app/utils/supabase/account.ts` filters on `dg_account` for a person session. No production person account has a `dg_account` yet.
  * Four website integration test files read their own `dg_account` as a space login.
  * The cucumber step "a user logged in space ... should see ... in the database" uses `select("*")`, which fails on `PlatformAccount`.
* Check for direct embeds of `PlatformAccount`, and for a bare `.select()` after a write. Both fail if they request a hidden column.

Proposed checks:

* A space peer can't read `dg_account` or `metadata` from `PlatformAccount`, and can't filter on them.
* A space peer still reads the listed columns.
* Row visibility and updates of `name` and `active` don't change.

**Required now?**

Not for today's data. It must land before the first claim, and it's cheapest now, while no client depends on these columns. A new `PlatformAccount` column, such as a claim's attestation level, also stays hidden until someone grants it.

**Anyone consulted?**

No one yet.

**Decision**

Include it in this ticket, unless a reviewer objects.

**Corrections to the current Solution**

* The migration must grant `EXECUTE` on `author_of_content` and `author_of_concept` to `anon` again. After ENG-2442, recreated functions no longer get that grant by default.
* The migration must sort after ENG-2442's migration. The commit on the branch still uses `20261008120000`.
* The branch is now `eng-2441-stop-my_accounts-from-exposing-auth-uids-and-metadata-to`.

**Evidence**

I tested the column list on a local database in a rolled-back transaction, as a space login, with two accounts. Reads of the listed columns, row visibility and updates by `id` worked. `select *`, reads of `dg_account` and filters on `dg_account` or `metadata` were denied. I didn't test through PostgREST or test the `metadata` revoke. The cucumber scenarios will cover this.

**Rules for later work**

* ENG-2444: `my_pseudo_accounts` returns `dg_account`, so it must stay a definer view.
* ENG-1837 and ENG-2444: any `anon` grant on `PlatformAccount` must use the same column list.
* ENG-2445: plugin reads of the table must name their columns.
* Discourse Graph accounts: column grants apply to all rows, so a person can't read their own claim from the table. Claim status needs a function or a view.

**Not covered**

* User ids stay readable in `SpaceAccess`, `ResourceAccess`, `group_membership` and `my_pseudo_accounts`. The [accounts spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/s86_P-XTI) explains why, with the pros and cons of hiding them.
* `AgentIdentifier.value` is readable from `reader` access. Where it holds an email, that email can also link one person's accounts across spaces.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-11-04T18:06:52.622Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-04T18:06:52.536Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null}],"hasNextPage":false}

**`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, as a logged-in user:** one run each, same data. `PlatformAccount` select: 808.13 → 8.91 ms. Account upsert: 2.92 → 3.00 ms, which is within noise (the upsert doesn't go through these policies).

Reading the table directly is now faster than `my_accounts` for batches of 100 or more, which supports moving those reads later.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-11-01T23:37:48.939Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-01T23:37:48.892Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"b27f3157-3767-4757-94e1-bcf069df9b93","body":"**Implementation finding:** Checks on readable spaces use a per-row `EXISTS` on `LocalAccess`, through its primary key, against a once-per-query list of the caller's spaces. The helper remains for the partial branch of the `PlatformAccount` select, and for `LocalAccess` and `AgentIdentifier` writes. Inside a policy, `LocalAccess` is filtered by its own reader-level select policy, so an inline check can't see partial access. A `LocalAccess` policy that queried `LocalAccess` would also recurse.

---
name: tickets-state-goals-not-methods
description: "Ticket drafts: Done When states goals, Solution offers an approach considered; a different method is an implementation finding, never room for more scope. Proposed guidance for dg-create-engineering-ticket, not applied."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: d9f6f7e7-e8d3-42e7-a56b-3302f54bdf81
  modified: 2026-11-05T00:46:21.577Z
---

When drafting tickets, don't over-specify the method. `Solution` should say what to change so the problem is solved, and offer the design as "one approach considered". `Done When` should be about goals, not method.

**Why:** stated 2026-11-01 on ENG-2446. Its Solution named exact helpers and policy shapes, and implementation found a better shape (per-row `LocalAccess` check for readable spaces). The over-precise body made a sound implementation choice look like a deviation that needed explaining.

**Applies when exploration is involved.** On 2026-11-04 the user flagged ENG-2461, whose Solution locked in an experimental engine, and accepted ENG-2459 and ENG-2460 naming their methods because "we presume there is no exploration involved there". So state aims plus a "potential solution" when the method is still open, and don't reword tickets whose fix is already settled.

**How to apply:**
- A changed method under such a ticket is an implementation finding, not scope: no scope note needed, at most a mention. See [[scope-change-taxonomy]].
- A missed goal in `Done When` is still a real gap and gets reported (ENG-2446's "neither is slower").
- Tickets already approved and older keep their text; record findings in a comment. See [[shared-docs-are-collective]].

**Proposed guidance for `dg-create-engineering-ticket`.** The user wants it kept here as guidance for now: don't edit the skill. Michael will worry about anything that reads as a way to expand scope, so the wording must make the boundary tighter or equal, never looser:

- `Done When` is the scope boundary. Write each item as the goal the change must reach, limited to this change, so a reviewer can verify it without knowing the implementation.
- `Solution` describes the smallest change considered. When the method isn't itself a requirement, present it as an approach considered.
- An implementer can use a different method only to reach the same `Done When`. A method that does more than `Done When` requires is still a scope expansion and follows the usual scope-check rules.
- Example: "This change leaves no unneeded function behind" instead of "Drop `a`, `b` and `c`". Keep "this change leaves": a bare "no unneeded function" could read as a cleanup of the whole schema.

name: db-reset-between-branches
description: "Before cucumber on another branch, run supabase db reset; migrations applied by hand with psql leave the local DB out of step with the branch."
metadata:

  modified: 2026-10-30T01:44:12.044Z

When cucumber runs on a branch other than the one whose migration was last applied by hand (psql -f), reset the local database from that branch's migrations first (`supabase db reset`, on `supabase_db_test`).

**Why:** on 2026-10-29 the ENG-2439 suite failed after ENG-2438's migration had been applied by psql, leaving a schema that matched neither branch; `db reset` fixed it. The exact failing step was never examined.

**How to apply:** treat a schema that doesn't match the branch as the first suspect when a previously green suite fails after a branch switch. Resetting wipes the database, so ask first, as with any cucumber run ([[never-run-cucumber-tests]]). Related: [[security-candidates-work-state]].

-- New functions are not executable without a login. Grant anon explicitly where a client or policy needs it.
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres IN SCHEMA public REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTIONS FROM anon;
-- PUBLIC gets EXECUTE on new functions by default, and anon inherits it. Only a global default, not a per-schema one, can remove it.
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM public;

-- Every role that calls our functions holds its own grant, so PUBLIC's grant only matters for anon.
-- Removing it makes existing functions match the ones created under the defaults above.
DO $$
DECLARE
    fn regprocedure;
BEGIN
    FOR fn IN
        SELECT p.oid::regprocedure FROM pg_catalog.pg_proc AS p
        WHERE p.pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace
        AND p.proowner = 'postgres'::regrole
        AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.pg_depend AS d
            WHERE d.classid = 'pg_catalog.pg_proc'::regclass AND d.objid = p.oid AND d.deptype = 'e'
        )
    LOOP
        EXECUTE format('REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION %s FROM PUBLIC', fn);
    END LOOP;
END;
$$;

  User story:

  * I want each function to be executable only by the roles that call it
  * So that a SECURITY DEFINER function cannot be called outside the flow it was written for

  Acceptance criteria:
  * Clients without a login get a permission error calling functions that only logged-in clients use
  * Clients without a login can still call the functions that their reads need
  * No client can call a function that only triggers use
  * Clients without a login cannot write to the contributor tables
  * The triggers still run when a logged-in client deletes rows

+-- The function bypasses RLS and checked no access, and its SpaceAccess branch would grant editor to any owned account.
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.upsert_account_in_space(
+    space_id_ BIGINT,
+    local_account public.account_local_input
+) RETURNS BIGINT
+SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = ''
+LANGUAGE plpgsql
+AS $$
+DECLARE
+    platform_ public."Platform";
+    account_id_ BIGINT;
+BEGIN
+    -- This function bypasses RLS, so it must check access itself.
+    IF NOT public.in_space(space_id_, 'editor') THEN
+        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Editor access to space % required', space_id_
+            USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege';
+    END IF;
+    SELECT platform INTO STRICT platform_ FROM public."Space" WHERE id = space_id_;
+    INSERT INTO public."PlatformAccount" AS pa (
+            account_local_id, name, platform
+        ) VALUES (
+            local_account.account_local_id, local_account.name, platform_
+        ) ON CONFLICT (account_local_id, platform) DO UPDATE SET
+            name = COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(EXCLUDED.name), ''), pa.name)
+        RETURNING id INTO STRICT account_id_;
+    INSERT INTO public."LocalAccess" (space_id, account_id) values (space_id_, account_id_)
+        ON CONFLICT (space_id, account_id)
+        DO NOTHING;
+    IF local_account.email IS NOT NULL THEN
+        -- TODO: how to distinguish basic untrusted from platform placeholder email?
+        INSERT INTO public."AgentIdentifier" as ai (account_id, value, identifier_type, trusted) VALUES (account_id_, local_account.email, 'email', COALESCE(local_account.email_trusted, false))
+        ON CONFLICT (value, identifier_type, account_id)
+        DO UPDATE SET trusted = COALESCE(local_account.email_trusted, ai.trusted, false);
+    END IF;
+    RETURN account_id_;
+END;
+$$;
+
+COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.upsert_account_in_space IS 'Add an account to a space the caller can edit. Grants no SpaceAccess: the space_editor and permissions fields of the input are ignored.';
+COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.upsert_accounts_in_space IS 'Add accounts to a space the caller can edit, through upsert_account_in_space.';
+COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.create_account_in_space IS 'Legacy wrapper of upsert_account_in_space; permissions_ is ignored.';

+REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.upsert_accounts_in_space(BIGINT, JSONB) FROM public, anon;
+REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.create_account_in_space(BIGINT, varchar, varchar, varchar, boolean, public."SpaceAccessPermissions") FROM public, anon;

1	##### today 2442 doc change
2	diff --git a/packages/database/doc/security_model.md b/packages/database/doc/security_model.md
3	index 403b3e6cf..f9d60ed2f 100644
4	--- a/packages/database/doc/security_model.md
5	+++ b/packages/database/doc/security_model.md
6	@@ -43,12 +43,14 @@ The `my_*` views (`my_spaces`, `my_accounts`, `my_concepts`, `my_contents`, `my_
7	 
8	 They are not `security_invoker`: they run as their owner, bypass RLS, and apply their own access filter. This was done for speed, when policies called their helpers once per row and large reads timed out (ENG-1433, ENG-1435). The views compute the user's accessible spaces once per query, in the InitPlan form above (ENG-2344, ENG-2359).
9	 
10	+The policies now use that form too, but most views stay definer, because they're still faster. Under RLS, a filter that isn't `LEAKPROOF` has to run after the policy, so it can't use an index. `concept_in_relations` filters with `@>`, and took about 250 times as long through RLS with 273 `ResourceAccess` rows. Reading the tables directly has the same cost. So by default, clients read through these views and write to the tables. The timings are on ENG-2444, which is parked.
11	+
12	 Consequences:
13	 
14	-- Each view's filter is a second copy of the table's access rules. A change to a policy must be repeated in the views that read the table. ENG-2444 covers moving the views to `security_invoker`.
15	+- Each view's filter is a second copy of the table's access rules. A change to a policy must be repeated in the views that read the table. We accept this cost, and the security advisor keeps reporting these views.
16	 - Single-table views are automatically updatable, and writes through them would also bypass RLS. Write privileges are revoked on `my_spaces`, `my_accounts`, `my_concepts`, `my_contents`, `my_documents` and `my_file_references` (ENG-2368, ENG-2359). Any new updatable view needs the same `REVOKE`.
17	 - Clients depend on the view names and columns, including older plugin versions that are still installed, PostgREST's foreign-key inference and the generated types. Keep them stable.
18	-- They have no `security_barrier`, so a caller's filter that isn't `LEAKPROOF` can run below the access filter and see rows the view would hide (measured on `my_accounts`). PostgREST's fixed filter operators shouldn't allow such a filter, so this matters for direct SQL access.
19	+- They have no `security_barrier`, so a caller's filter that isn't `LEAKPROOF` can run below the access filter and see rows the view would hide (measured on `my_accounts`). PostgREST's fixed filter operators shouldn't allow such a filter, so this matters for direct SQL access. The same reordering is what lets `@>` use its index, so time the relation queries before adding `security_barrier` to `my_concepts`.
20	 
21	 ## Function grants
22	 
23	@@ -100,7 +102,7 @@ It flags any view that bypasses RLS, any view that reads `auth.users`, any polic
24	 - The other eight `my_*` views (`security_definer_view`). This is the speed workaround described above.
25	 - `accounts_in_my_partial_spaces` (`security_definer_view`). It runs as its owner on purpose, to read `LocalAccess` below `reader` (see above). It stays.
26	 - `anon_security_definer_function_executable` for the four functions in the table above.
27	-- `authenticated_security_definer_function_executable` for the policy helpers and for the functions that clients call directly: `create_account_in_space`, `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space`, `file_exists`, `create_secret_token`, `get_secret_token`, `accept_group_invitation`.
28	+- `authenticated_security_definer_function_executable` for the policy helpers and for the functions that clients call directly: `create_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space`, `file_exists`, `create_secret_token`, `get_secret_token`, `accept_group_invitation`. Also for `upsert_account_in_space`: no client calls it, but `upsert_content` and `upsert_documents` run as the caller, so the caller needs `EXECUTE`.
29	 - `space_insert_policy` on `Space` (`rls_policy_always_true`). Any new user of the plugins must be able to create their own space, so the insert policy is `WITH CHECK (true)`. Reading, changing and deleting a space still require access to it: those policies check `my_space_ids`.
30	 
31	 ### Performance advisor
32	##### 2442 migration
33	-- New functions are not executable without a login. Grant anon explicitly where a client or policy needs it.
34	ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres IN SCHEMA public REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTIONS FROM anon;
35	-- PUBLIC gets EXECUTE on new functions by default, and anon inherits it. Only a global default, not a per-schema one, can remove it.
36	ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM public;
37	
38	-- Every role that calls our functions holds its own grant, so PUBLIC's grant only matters for anon.
39	-- Removing it makes existing functions match the ones created under the defaults above.
40	DO $$
41	DECLARE
42	    fn regprocedure;
43	BEGIN
44	    FOR fn IN
45	        SELECT p.oid::regprocedure FROM pg_catalog.pg_proc AS p
46	        WHERE p.pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace
47	        AND p.proowner = 'postgres'::regrole
48	        AND NOT EXISTS (
49	            SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.pg_depend AS d
50	            WHERE d.classid = 'pg_catalog.pg_proc'::regclass AND d.objid = p.oid AND d.deptype = 'e'
51	        )
52	    LOOP
53	        EXECUTE format('REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION %s FROM PUBLIC', fn);
54	    END LOOP;
55	END;
56	$$;
57	
58	-- Only triggers call these. Postgres checks EXECUTE on a trigger function when the trigger is created, not when it fires.
59	REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.after_delete_space() FROM anon, authenticated;
60	REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.after_delete_update_fref() FROM anon, authenticated;
61	REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.after_insert_fref() FROM anon, authenticated;
62	REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.on_delete_local_reference() FROM anon, authenticated;
63	REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.on_update_local_reference() FROM anon, authenticated;
64	REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.on_delete_space_revoke_local_access() FROM anon, authenticated;
65	REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.concept_set_derived_columns() FROM anon, authenticated;
66	REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.concept_propagate_derived_columns() FROM anon, authenticated;
67	REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.is_last_local_reference(bigint, varchar) FROM anon, authenticated;

# ENG-2438 PR notes (held: security fix)

Branch `eng-2438-stop-users-from-joining-another-users-space-access-through-a`, head `baf2ef84f`, on `main`. Not on the stack. Ticket: https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2438/stop-users-from-joining-another-users-space-access-through-a-group

## Left before the PR

1. Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check`. It has never run on this branch.
2. Run `$scope-check`, and post the ticket comment below, so the scope line can cite it.
3. Rerun the delegated review. The October 29 review covered the fix commit (`6d37d593a`, no findings), not the blank-step commit or the rebase on `main`.
4. Rerun the full cucumber suite and `pnpm ci:validate` on the head. The last recorded suite is 36 of 36 on October 29, before the rebase.
5. Ticket Notes still name the old branch `security-group-membership-insert`. The ticket is approved, so correct this in a comment if at all.

## Landing with the stack

The PR can target `main`, which gives a clean diff. Before it lands with the stack:

- Re-date `20261029130000`, which sorts before every stack migration.
- Trial merge onto the ENG-2441 head conflicts in `account.sql` (keep the `is_group_admin` revoke and comment, drop the `group_exists` block) and `stepdefs.ts` (keep both sides).
- Regenerate `dbTypes`, add its `security_model.md` lines from `doc/security_model.future.md`, and recheck that both scenarios fail under the old rule.

ENG-2442's guard on `group_exists` allows either order.

## Manual tests

None needed. Cucumber covers `create-group` and `accept_group_invitation`, and the website invitation flow is one of ENG-2442's live checks.

After the migration is applied in production, run `packages/database/eng-2438-abuse-check.sql` (read-only, untracked). It has only run on an empty database, so check its sanity query first.

## Loom

Explain the code, plus a before and after:

- The old policy's `OR NOT group_exists(group_id)` and why it passes for any user id that is not yet a group.
- Before: under the old policy, `groupMembership.feature` fails on both scenarios (a reader joining an editor's id, and joining an emptied group).
- After: both pass.
- Why nothing needs the removed clause: `create-group` uses the service role, and `accept_group_invitation` is a security definer.
- What remains: a group admin can still add any known user id, which ENG-2456 covers.

## Ticket comment to post (scope)

The cucumber step "the database is blank" now finds groups through `auth.admin.listUsers`, by their `user_metadata.group` flag, instead of through `group_membership`. This ticket adds the first scenario that empties a group. The old step missed groups with no members, and they broke later runs. The change touches only test code.

## Draft PR body

Title: `ENG-2438 Stop users from joining another user's space access through a group membership`

Base: `main`

```markdown
## Reviewer brief

- Result: only a group's admins can add members. A client can no longer add itself to a group by naming any user id that isn't yet a group, or a group whose last member left.

Reading all visible accounts at 20,020 accounts goes from about 826 ms to 10 ms, and renaming 100 accounts from 973 ms to 18 ms. Partial access goes through the definer view `accounts_in_my_partial_spaces`, because a policy's read of `LocalAccess` is filtered by that table's reader-level select policy, and the planner can inline a view but not a function with `SET search_path`. The view keeps `DISTINCT` and `security_barrier` so that it reveals no memberships. `ROWS 10` on `my_user_accounts` stops the planner from scanning `SpaceAccess`.
- Risk or follow-up: reading the `AgentIdentifier` rows of one account is slightly slower, 0.41 to 0.46 ms. `my_accounts` has no `security_barrier`, and this PR doesn't change that.

## Verification

- `features/accountTableAccess.feature`: the visibility and write scenarios passed on the policies before the change, and pass after it.
- Old and new policies gave the same results in 1,324 probes across partial, reader and editor access, direct and through groups. They ran on the final policies, in a rolled-back transaction.

Head `bb40fac01`.

1. Rerun `$dg-pr-adherence-check` and the delegated review, and confirm `$scope-check`. The review and the adherence check ran on October 30, before the November 3 change that revokes `INSERT` and drops the insert policy. Those two boxes are unchecked below until they run on the final diff.

4. Run the production check for claims and forged rows from the ticket's Notes. The SQL isn't written yet, and it belongs before the batch is applied.

## Manual tests

Done When lists space creation among what must keep working. Cucumber creates spaces directly, so it doesn't run `create-space`. These are part of the same pass as ENG-2442's live checks, at the ENG-2441 head:

1. Connect a fresh Roam graph and a fresh Obsidian vault. `create-space` runs, then `create_account_in_space` as the new login.

3. Run a Roam sync that adds an author. `upsert_accounts_in_space` still creates accounts, although clients can no longer insert them directly.

## Loom

Explain the code, plus a before and after:

- The two problems, in order: who owns an account, then which space a `LocalAccess` row names.

---
name: cucumber-skips-create-space
description: "Corrected 2026-11-05: cucumber DOES run the create-space edge function, through fetchOrCreateSpaceDirect in the 'opens the plugin' step. An earlier note said the opposite."
metadata:
  type: project
---

Cucumber's "the user ... opens the ... plugin in space ..." step calls `fetchOrCreateSpaceDirect`, which invokes the `create-space` edge function, then `fetchOrCreatePlatformAccount`, which calls `create_account_in_space` as the new login. It has done so since 2025 (`992296392`). So a green run does exercise `create-space`.

**Why:** this note used to claim the reverse, and that claim spread: I repeated it in PR notes on 2026-11-05 and caught it reading `contextFunctions.ts`. It also appears in comment c220df10 on ENG-2442 and in Roam candidate kr33IACmG, neither of which I changed.

**How to apply:** for `create-space` changes, cucumber is real evidence. A plugin call adds only what the plugin itself does (browser headers, CORS). What cucumber doesn't reach: storage, sync tasks, schema updates, the website's token handoff. See [[never-run-cucumber-tests]].

Cucumber's "the user ... opens the ... plugin in space ..." step calls `fetchOrCreateSpaceDirect`, which invokes the `create-space` edge function, then `fetchOrCreatePlatformAccount`, which calls `create_account_in_space` as the new login. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.

- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.

## Return the result

Return a copy-ready section:

```markdown
## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
```

The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. cd /Users/maparent/OpenSource/discourse-graph; S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maparent-OpenSource-discourse-graph/0c545272-5f06-45ba-988c-08ee1a192915/scratchpad
grep -n -A16 'schema_paths' packages/database/supabase/config.toml | head -28
cat > $S/schema_build.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Builds a throwaway database from the schema files and diffs function and table ACLs against the migrated postgres database.
S=$1; TAG=$2; R=/Users/maparent/OpenSource/discourse-graph
[ "$(docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep _db_)" = "supabase_db_test" ] || { echo WRONG DB; exit 1; }
A="docker exec -i supabase_db_test psql -U supabase_admin"
P="docker exec -i supabase_db_test psql -U postgres"
$A -d postgres -q -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS schema_build" -c "CREATE DATABASE schema_build TEMPLATE template0 OWNER postgres"
docker exec supabase_db_test pg_dump -U supabase_admin -s -N public postgres > $S/base_$TAG.sql
$A -d schema_build -q < $S/base_$TAG.sql > $S/base_load_$TAG.txt 2>&1
# State a fresh Supabase project has before base.sql runs. The dump carries the migrations' default privileges, so these undo that.
$A -d schema_build -q <<'SQL' > $S/init_$TAG.txt 2>&1
GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO postgres, anon, authenticated, service_role;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS TO PUBLIC;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON FUNCTIONS TO anon, authenticated, service_role;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO anon, authenticated, service_role;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON SEQUENCES TO anon, authenticated, service_role;
SQL
cd $R/packages/database/supabase
: > $S/schema_load_$TAG.txt
for f in $(python3 -I -c "
import re
t=open('config.toml').read()
m=re.search(r'schema_paths\s*=\s*\[(.*?)\]',t,re.S)
print(' '.join(re.findall(r'\"([^\"]+)\"',m.group(1))))"); do
  echo "--- $f" >> $S/schema_load_$TAG.txt
  $P -d schema_build -q < $f >> $S/schema_load_$TAG.txt 2>&1
done
Q="SELECT p.oid::regprocedure::text, coalesce((SELECT string_agg(CASE a.grantee WHEN 0 THEN 'PUBLIC' ELSE a.grantee::regrole::text END, ',' ORDER BY 1) FROM aclexplode(coalesce(p.proacl, acldefault('f',p.proowner))) a WHERE a.privilege_type='EXECUTE'),'') FROM pg_proc p WHERE p.pronamespace='public'::regnamespace AND p.proowner='postgres'::regrole AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_depend d WHERE d.classid='pg_proc'::regclass AND d.objid=p.oid AND d.deptype='e') ORDER BY 1"
T="SELECT c.relkind||' '||c.relname, coalesce((SELECT string_agg(a.grantee::regrole::text||':'||a.privilege_type, ',' ORDER BY 1) FROM aclexplode(coalesce(c.relacl, acldefault(CASE WHEN c.relkind='S' THEN 's'::\"char\" ELSE 'r'::\"char\" END,c.relowner))) a WHERE a.grantee<>0),'') FROM pg_class c WHERE c.relnamespace='public'::regnamespace AND c.relkind IN ('r','v','S','m') ORDER BY 1"
$P -d postgres -AtF'|' -c "$Q" > $S/fn_mig_$TAG.txt; $P -d schema_build -AtF'|' -c "$Q" > $S/fn_sch_$TAG.txt
$P -d postgres -AtF'|' -c "$T" > $S/tb_mig_$TAG.txt; $P -d schema_build -AtF'|' -c "$T" > $S/tb_sch_$TAG.txt
echo "functions: migrated $(wc -l <$S/fn_mig_$TAG.txt), schema-built $(wc -l <$S/fn_sch_$TAG.txt)"
echo "tables/views/seqs: migrated $(wc -l <$S/tb_mig_$TAG.txt), schema-built $(wc -l <$S/tb_sch_$TAG.txt)"
echo "schema load errors: $(grep -c ERROR $S/schema_load_$TAG.txt)"; grep -n ERROR $S/schema_load_$TAG.txt | head -12 | cut -c1-170
echo "--- function ACL diff (< migrated, > schema)"; diff $S/fn_mig_$TAG.txt $S/fn_sch_$TAG.txt | cut -c1-190 | head -40
echo "--- table ACL diff (< migrated, > schema)"; diff $S/tb_mig_$TAG.txt $S/tb_sch_$TAG.txt | cut -c1-230 | head -30
$A -d postgres -q -c "DROP DATABASE schema_build"
EOF
git branch --show-current; bash $S/schema_build.sh $S 2441 2>&1 | tail -80
input.description: Build a throwaway database from schema files and diff its grants against migrations

# DG Delegated Full Review

Use this skill only when the user invokes it directly or an explicitly requested workflow invokes it. Do not select it automatically.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. Look for it in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

May be selected by `$*-run-scoped-engineering-workflow` at step 6 through its review dispatcher. Standalone use remains supported. This skill owns the single review subagent; never route back through the personal dispatcher. Preserve any caller-supplied acceptance boundary alongside the review target.

## Resolve the target

- Preserve a pull request, branch, commit, diff, or other review target supplied by the user.
- Otherwise, review all staged, unstaged, and untracked changes in the current working directory.
- If the working tree is clean, review the current branch against its merge base with the configured upstream or default base branch.

Report only concrete, actionable regressions introduced by the change. List findings by severity with precise file and line references. If there are no qualifying findings, return "No findings." Do not modify files or delegate the review.

## Close the review task

- In Codex, close the completed subagent when a non-destructive close or archive action is available. Otherwise report that the runtime does not support cleanup.
- Claude Code subagents are ephemeral and need no separate archive action.
