# [[Supabase]] Warnings <roam uid="ievzCqZRG" refs="4"/>

- From: <roam uid="hJ39Olwz-"/>
  - [Security advisor](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security) <roam uid="lt-K2bOHW"/>
  - [Performance advisor](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/performance) <roam uid="x9cl5YBsH"/>
- Record a decision (**keep**, **fix**, **not applicable**, or **investigate**) and the reason, evidence, or follow-up ticket. A shared explanation must name the findings it covers. <roam uid="REsCRA2jz"/>
- Snapshots <roam uid="0o15VZttL"/>
  - [[October 27th, 2026]] <roam uid="iNDyvdcK0"/>
    - 84 findings across 10 types: 10 errors, 60 warnings, 14 informational notices. <roam uid="GroESo50B"/>
    - Counts overlap: each of 27 functions has two findings; `my_groups` has two findings. <roam uid="wxNW4BHhJ"/>
  - October 29, 2026, from CSV exports of the security and performance advisors: 10 errors, 61 warnings and 14 informational notices. They match the page, plus one warning that wasn't listed (`rls_policy_always_true` on `Space`, now added). <roam uid="FJeGlULLb"/>
- **Errors (10)** <roam uid="TAbkQd0Xu" refs="1"/>
  - **Exposed auth users (1)** <roam uid="dI7SeSOwP" refs="1"/>
    - [public.my_groups](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=ERROR&id=auth_users_exposed_public_my_groups) · `auth_users_exposed` · [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/database-linter?lint=0002_auth_users_exposed) <roam uid="89_ea8gP6"/>
    - Reads IDs and email-derived names from `auth.users`, filtered by `group_membership.member_id = auth.uid()`. Owned by `postgres`; `anon` and `authenticated` have SELECT. API access hasn't been tested. <roam uid="6Nm55U8qg"/>
    - Context: [ENG-1284](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1284/view-showing-groups-a-user-is-part-of) (**Released**), [PR #741](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/741), explains the group lookup's need to access `auth.users`. It doesn't justify anonymous access. <roam uid="bRjyIS0Wd"/>
    - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. The view returns only the id and name of the groups the current user belongs to; a request without a login gets no rows. ((9fxx9mOK-))<ref>'my_groups' reads 'auth.users' (2 errors: **Exposed auth users (1)** and **Security-definer views (9->10)**)</ref> <roam uid="idRwDEwXr"/>
      - from [discord](https://discord.com/channels/1313599657800110202/1493690942685839430) <roam uid="hv3tyoJ6Y"/>
        - img <roam uid="0bR8IQaqo"/>
          - ![](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FCcnrYsmqd7.png?alt=media&token=a19cb5be-bab0-43c2-b8f6-f6e1413a2969) <roam uid="mjED2pDvZ"/>
        - > Quote from the issue: \n\n---\nView/Materialized View "my_groups" in the public schema may expose auth.users data to anon or authenticated roles.\nDescription\n\nDetects if auth.users is exposed to anon or authenticated roles via a view or materialized view in schemas exposed to PostgREST, potentially compromising user data security.\n---\n\nAnd indeed, my_groups shows you pseudo-users that correspond to groups you're part of. That is a well-controlled exposure, but the automated warning is too simple to check for that. <roam uid="tOp7hC4rU"/>
  - **Security-definer views (9->10)** <roam uid="3e4nCiOPH" refs="3"/>
    - `security_definer_view`: views use their creator's permissions and RLS context. [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/database-linter?lint=0010_security_definer_view) <roam uid="Fc-UTrk6q"/>
    - All views below are in `public`. <roam uid="fjyqqb70u"/>
    - [my_contents](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=ERROR&id=security_definer_view_public_my_contents) <roam uid="5WI6Sdisa" refs="1"/>
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. `getConcepts` with content is about 14 times slower through RLS ((YOKc48ben))<ref>2. Security-definer views we keep for now: 8 errors, most of them for speed</ref>. ENG-2444 is in Icebox. <roam uid="GP6w1Xw5k"/>
    - [my_pseudo_accounts](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=ERROR&id=security_definer_view_public_my_pseudo_accounts) <roam uid="bVPIvT8yX" refs="1"/>
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. It returns `dg_account`, which clients can't read from the table after ENG-2441. <roam uid="f45dTb0Yz"/>
    - [my_contents_with_embedding_openai_text_embedding_3_small_1536](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=ERROR&id=security_definer_view_public_my_contents_with_embedding_openai_text_embedding_3_small_1536) <roam uid="42c4knWt5" refs="1"/>
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. Reads are up to about 4 times slower through RLS as data grows, and the policy has to check `Content` for each row ((YOKc48ben))<ref>2. Security-definer views we keep for now: 8 errors, most of them for speed</ref>. ENG-2444 is in Icebox. <roam uid="S8j7DZY50"/>
    - [my_accounts](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=ERROR&id=security_definer_view_public_my_accounts) <roam uid="_Vkv3sRz1" refs="2"/>
      - [ENG-1480](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1480/supabase-security-advisor-error-security-definer-view) (**Backlog / Low**): Marc-Antoine said the views apply the same access logic globally to avoid row-by-row RLS costs. Tighter access remained worth testing. <roam uid="VTdxyQJ1E"/>
      - [ENG-2368](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2368/revoke-write-privileges-on-the-my-spaces-and-my-accounts-views) (**Released**) revoked write privileges on `my_accounts` and `my_spaces`; this remaining warning concerns definer behavior. <roam uid="U4ip888UB"/>
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. ENG-1837 needs this view to show `anonymous #<id>` instead of a real name for accounts seen only through a public grant. RLS can select rows but can't change a column's value. Explained in a comment on ENG-2444. <roam uid="ISLuW7moB"/>
    - [my_concepts](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=ERROR&id=security_definer_view_public_my_concepts) <roam uid="0SPFE6ncu" refs="1"/>
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. `concept_in_relations` is about 250 times slower through RLS ((YOKc48ben))<ref>2. Security-definer views we keep for now: 8 errors, most of them for speed</ref>. ENG-2444 is in Icebox. <roam uid="c9AN14DTi"/>
    - [my_documents](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=ERROR&id=security_definer_view_public_my_documents) <roam uid="DGuMemdwG" refs="1"/>
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. Listings are about 23% to 32% slower through RLS, around the 25% limit ((YOKc48ben))<ref>2. Security-definer views we keep for now: 8 errors, most of them for speed</ref>. `getConcepts` reads it inside the content embed, so it would have to change together with `my_contents`. ENG-2444 is in Icebox. <roam uid="mw9mQZHYm"/>
    - [my_spaces](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=ERROR&id=security_definer_view_public_my_spaces) <roam uid="Ee0stb6_p"/>
      - [ENG-2368](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2368/revoke-write-privileges-on-the-my-spaces-and-my-accounts-views) (**Released**) revoked write privileges on `my_accounts` and `my_spaces`; this remaining warning concerns definer behavior. <roam uid="HSRr820Pu"/>
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **fix, low priority**. This is the only view that passes: faster through RLS (0.88 ms to 0.07 ms), with no rule it needs to keep for itself. Not worth its own PR, so ENG-2444 is in Icebox. Convert it when someone is working in that code. <roam uid="74GEf5Fqa"/>
    - [my_file_references](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=ERROR&id=security_definer_view_public_my_file_references) <roam uid="JB3q61GSh" refs="1"/>
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. Listings are up to 87% slower through RLS ((YOKc48ben))<ref>2. Security-definer views we keep for now: 8 errors, most of them for speed</ref>. ENG-2444 is in Icebox. <roam uid="3ZkqG7Ik8"/>
    - [my_groups](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=ERROR&id=security_definer_view_public_my_groups) <roam uid="UKN26fJCh" refs="1"/>
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. It must run with the owner's rights, because users can't read `auth.users`. ((9fxx9mOK-))<ref>'my_groups' reads 'auth.users' (2 errors: **Exposed auth users (1)** and **Security-definer views (9->10)**)</ref> <roam uid="9QmBggTKa"/>
    - [accounts_in_my_partial_spaces](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=ERROR&id=security_definer_view_public_accounts_in_my_partial_spaces) <roam uid="csxt8PwtR"/>
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. It was introduced for RLS optimizations. BUT it could be hidden using ((QMPLUito7))<ref>Move internal database functions and views out of 'public', into a schema PostgREST doesn't expose #iss-candidate</ref> <roam uid="banZl7UvQ"/>
        - {{[[DONE]]}} [[Marc-Antoine Parent]] Todo Add the  new utility definer view, and link to ((QMPLUito7))<ref>Move internal database functions and views out of 'public', into a schema PostgREST doesn't expose #iss-candidate</ref> <roam uid="l1-PBIpRk"/>
- **Warnings (61->23)** <roam uid="bbwyrY-Ar" refs="1"/>
  - **Extension in public (1)** <roam uid="4OAIH89I3"/>
    - [public.pg_stat_monitor](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=WARN&id=extension_in_public_pg_stat_monitor) · `extension_in_public` · [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/database-linter?lint=0014_extension_in_public) <roam uid="PsQ7bw2Pw"/>
    - Decision / reason / evidence:: fix. The schema and migrations both say this should live in extensions; it was almost certainly a mistake done by hand in the supabase UI. <roam uid="9Z1yG-Kr1"/>
      - [ENG-2459: Remove `pg_cron` from `extensions.sql` and move `pg_stat_monitor` to the `extensions` schema in production​](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2459/remove-pg-cron-from-extensionssql-and-move-pg-stat-monitor-to-the) <roam uid="mp2DAwsNU"/>
      - Tested on a local database, in a transaction that was rolled back: the extension is relocatable, and `ALTER EXTENSION pg_stat_monitor SET SCHEMA public` and then `SET SCHEMA extensions` both worked. In production, `ALTER EXTENSION pg_stat_monitor SET SCHEMA extensions;` should be enough, with no drop and no loss of statistics. <roam uid="aD7LP79Li"/>
  - **Email OTP expiry (1)** <roam uid="wOZ92Nnhq" refs="1"/>
    - Expiry exceeds one hour; exact duration 1d. `auth_otp_long_expiry` · [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/going-into-prod#security) · [Email OTP settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/auth/providers) <roam uid="Jih2-n8SV"/>
    - Decision / reason / evidence:: Investigate. This concerns discourse graph accounts, how much should the "validate user" link sent by email last? Supabase recommends a 1h limit, we had set it to 1d in `packages/database/supabase/config.toml`, I don't remember that we thought about it so much. I would lean fix, very weakly. Follow-up: ((RKcaMnnB-))<ref>Decide how long email confirmation links and codes should stay valid #iss-candidate</ref> <roam uid="isgfoi-On"/>
  - **RLS policy always true (1)** <roam uid="kr2Aw5sB-"/>
    - [public.Space: space_insert_policy](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=WARN&id=rls_policy_always_true_public_Space_space_insert_policy) · `rls_policy_always_true` · [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/database-linter?lint=0024_permissive_rls_policy) <roam uid="q3jKnSHYR"/>

- Why Supabase flags our database, and what we can change <roam uid="MyX7CzumH"/>
  - **Why it matters:** Supabase's security advisor reports 10 errors and 54 function warnings on our database (snapshot of October 27, 2026). Some come from deliberate choices that stay. Some come from views that we keep, most of them for speed. The rest are mistakes that we can fix. This page sorts them so each decision on the [[[[Supabase]] Warnings]] page can point to a reason. <roam uid="9it2MD2rD"/>
  - Scope: the 10 errors, the 54 security-definer function warnings and the 4 repeated-auth-check warnings. The other warnings and the informational notices are not covered here. <roam uid="v1lNKiUcn"/>
  - Background <roam uid="NnwVHWM8d"/>
    - Row-level security (RLS) is how Postgres decides which rows each user can read or write. Each table has policies, and Postgres checks them for every row a query touches. <roam uid="HS-ADpXMA"/>
    - Our policies call helper functions such as `my_space_ids('reader')` ("which spaces can the current user access?"). These helpers are `SECURITY DEFINER`: they run with the database owner's rights, so they can read the access tables, which users can't read directly. <roam uid="fHOTihzKr"/>
    - Supabase has two roles that matter here. `anon` is any request made with the public API key and no login. `authenticated` is any logged-in request. Our plugins log in as a space's "anonymous" account, which uses the `authenticated` role, not `anon`. <roam uid="wBiEWDIsU"/>
    - Supabase's advisor checks shapes, not behaviour. It flags any view that bypasses RLS, any view that reads `auth.users`, and any `SECURITY DEFINER` function that a role can execute. It can't tell whether the function or view leaks anything. <roam uid="tuQTfUqya"/>
  - 1. Findings that stay <roam uid="tdD-ESJvb"/>
    - `my_groups` reads `auth.users` (2 errors: ((dI7SeSOwP))<ref>**Exposed auth users (1)**</ref> and ((3e4nCiOPH))<ref>**Security-definer views (9->10)**</ref>) <roam uid="9fxx9mOK-" refs="2"/>
      - Groups are rows in Supabase's `auth.users` table, with a made-up email `{group name}@groups.discoursegraphs.com` (set by the `create-group` function). Group management needs to show users the groups they belong to. <roam uid="BglrYKtOs"/>
      - The view returns only each group's id and name (the part of the email before the `@`), and only for groups the current user is a member of. A request without a login gets no rows. <roam uid="hFV3C9RTW"/>
      - It has to run with the owner's rights, because users can't read `auth.users` themselves. So both findings stay. Background: ENG-1284. <roam uid="-fITlDZK-"/>
    - Functions that stay executable (21 function warnings after the security batch) <roam uid="gyAe5u12c"/>
      - The 21 are: 9 policy helpers and `upsert_account_in_space` for `authenticated`, 7 functions that the plugins and website call directly for `authenticated`, and 4 functions for `anon`. <roam uid="z3fTaCoir"/>
      - The 7 called directly add accounts to a space, check whether a file was already uploaded, create and redeem tokens, accept group invitations, and list the caller's own accounts. Logged-in clients need them. The functions that add accounts get an access check first (section 3). <roam uid="YNQK-4EVf" refs="6"/>
      - Postgres requires the role making a query to have EXECUTE on every function its policies call. If we revoke a helper from a role, that role's queries on the table fail with a permission error. So every policy helper must stay executable by `authenticated`. <roam uid="0gzgKtI0D" refs="7"/>
      - The helpers are safe to call directly because they answer about the current user: "which spaces can I access?", "am I in this group?", "can I read this resource?". A direct call tells the caller nothing they couldn't learn by querying the table. <roam uid="S09P2Z4SC"/>
      - Some helpers must also stay executable by `anon`: <roam uid="WG1w3NUmn"/>
        - Needed today: `my_space_ids`, because `anon` can query `Space`, whose select policy calls it. Also `get_secret_token`, which the website calls to hand a plugin's session to a browser that isn't logged in yet. That token is 12 random bytes, single use, and expires after 45 seconds. <roam uid="rXlwYDJX_" refs="2"/>
        - Needed for public nodes: `my_user_accounts`, `my_space_ids` and `file_access`. Visitors without a login will read public nodes and their files through these functions (ENG-1837 and the planned public account). Revoking them now would mean granting them back. <roam uid="I_BUgWwN2" refs="3"/>
      - We will later want to show some author details on public nodes to visitors, so that author information becomes public only when its owner decides. How that works belongs with [[Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts]]. Until then, public readers see `anonymous #<id>` for authors. <roam uid="ayYZNwhGi" refs="1"/>
  - 2. Security-definer views we keep for now: 8 errors, most of them for speed <roam uid="YOKc48ben" refs="6"/>
    - **Why it matters:** these 8 errors come from views that apply our access rules themselves, instead of letting RLS do it. We tested replacing them with RLS, and most got slower, one of them by about 2,700 times. So most of these errors stay, and we accept that. See the timings on ENG-2444. <roam uid="MSLzXF5Cf"/>
    - Views: `my_accounts`, `my_spaces`, `my_concepts`, `my_contents`, `my_documents`, `my_file_references`, `my_contents_with_embedding_openai_text_embedding_3_small_1536`, `my_pseudo_accounts`. <roam uid="5KzD-hhLg"/>
    - Why they exist: our policies called a helper like `in_space` for every row. On large reads, such as a sync or a listing, that cost caused timeouts (ENG-1433, ENG-1435, ENG-950). The views compute the user's accessible spaces once per query and filter on that, bypassing RLS. On a local database, a direct read of `Concept` took 114.5 ms; the same read through `my_concepts` took 2.5 ms. <roam uid="LP4PN7ra_"/>
    - What Supabase objects to: a view that bypasses RLS holds a second copy of the access rules, and the two copies can drift apart. Single-table views were also writable, so writes through them skipped RLS. ENG-2368 and ENG-2359 closed that by revoking writes on the views. <roam uid="QZN05PpFt"/>
    - What we now know: per-row helper calls were a large part of the cost. Postgres doesn't reuse a function's result from one row to the next, so a helper in a filter runs once per row. Wrapping a call that doesn't depend on the row in `(SELECT ...)` makes Postgres compute it once per query. ENG-2344 used this inside `my_concepts` and cut a listing from 232.5 ms to 2.4 ms. ENG-2443 does this for the policies, so direct table reads and writes get faster. The views stay definer anyway, for the reasons below. <roam uid="Gfwy2ns1w"/>
    - What we measured, with synthetic data at production's 273 `ResourceAccess` rows (ENG-2444): <roam uid="M_EE2aFUn"/>
      - `concept_in_relations` goes from 10 ms to 2,500 ms for 100 nodes, through `security_invoker` views and through the tables. Its filter uses `@>`, which isn't `LEAKPROOF`, so under RLS the policy has to run first and the `refs` index can't be used. <roam uid="VGz7hgcDO"/>
      - `getConcepts` with content goes from 7 ms to about 100 ms. We haven't found out why. <roam uid="LIAvbGAVG"/>
      - Listings get 20-90% slower, over the ticket's 25% limit. <roam uid="8JIdSFkws"/>
      - Gains only appear around 100 times today's `ResourceAccess` size. <roam uid="cW6dj3Qjq"/>
      - The tables aren't a way around this. They go through the same RLS, and some embeds only exist for the views (ENG-2445). <roam uid="Q8cwv_cdp"/>
    - These views can't convert for reasons other than speed: `my_accounts` and `my_pseudo_accounts`, explained in their decisions under ((3e4nCiOPH))<ref>**Security-definer views (9->10)**</ref>. <roam uid="3SVpSlDIO"/>

    - Need / Problem Statement <roam uid="35gL4h2Z9"/>
      - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="aRPKlRvSS"/>
        - The problem is: email codes and links stay valid for 1 day, and Supabase recommends at most 1 hour. We don't remember choosing 1 day on purpose. Supabase flags this as `auth_otp_long_expiry`. <roam uid="L9poJnm2l"/>

    - Need / Problem Statement <roam uid="s6-0zHweC"/>
      - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="cI0Pl8Y0S"/>
        - The problem is: `base.sql` grants `ALL` to `anon` on every new table and sequence in `public`, and row-level security is off until someone enables it. So a new table is readable and writable by anyone without a login until its author restricts it. Forgetting one step exposes the table, and no test would catch it. <roam uid="0R_gz7AqZ"/>
        - ENG-2442 fixed the same default for functions. Tables and sequences still have it. <roam uid="_e9IRbcG1"/>
      - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them? <roam uid="Kr7vQoltj"/>
        - Anyone adding a table. Today each table is safe only because its schema file revokes `anon` by hand, and `security_model.md` lists that as a checklist item. <roam uid="LBJYjSwEM"/>
        - `Space` is the one table that still grants `ALL` to `anon`, on purpose in `space.sql`. See the evidence below. <roam uid="G_lyGrm0Z"/>
      - What request, observation, or other evidence supports this? <roam uid="krMHjSF5K"/>

        - Today's tables look safe: every other table in `public` revokes `anon`, and the contributor tables then grant back `SELECT` only. <roam uid="F0l5kqjq8"/>
        - `Space`: in the same kind of test, `anon` inserted a row. `anon` then saw 0 rows, and its update and delete changed nothing, because those policies need access to the space. So someone without a login can add junk rows to `Space`, but gets no access to any space. This was run as the `anon` role in SQL, not through the API. <roam uid="bMvvhkDUi"/>
        - `anon` also holds `TRUNCATE` on `Space`, which RLS doesn't limit. PostgREST doesn't offer `TRUNCATE`, so no route to it is known. ((E9_NZrWH9))<ref>Revoke TRUNCATE, TRIGGER and REFERENCES on public tables from anon and authenticated #iss-candidate</ref> covers that privilege for all tables. <roam uid="K0Iv-IzD2"/>
    - Proposed approach <roam uid="OXxxJ_RF4"/>
      - Revoke the default grants for `anon` on tables and sequences in `base.sql`, as ENG-2442 did for functions. Check for a second default that also gives them to `anon`, as there was for functions. Existing tables keep their explicit grants. <roam uid="HsPRc4g-a"/>
      - Reduce `anon` on `Space` to what it uses. `create-space` reads `Space` with the caller's key to check that key, so `anon` keeps `SELECT`. Its writes go through the service key, and the plugins call `create-space`, so `anon` shouldn't need `INSERT`. To confirm: no other client inserts into `Space` without a login. <roam uid="5mg3oGME3"/>
      - Add a scenario that lists what `anon` can do on each table in `public`, so a new table that is too open fails a test. <roam uid="TVS1L5-Sc"/>
      - ENG-1837 adds its grants explicitly, so it shouldn't conflict. <roam uid="qjGE-JINQ"/>

      - ^^What accepted user, developer, or project need would this address?^^ <roam uid="_NM5zjqud"/>
        - A new table is closed until someone opens it on purpose. <roam uid="naVwILgUF"/>
      - Is it relevant to work expected within the next six months? <roam uid="pJFm9Gl5U"/>
        - Yes. Each new table is another chance to forget, and public access makes `anon` a role we use on purpose. <roam uid="2Jt1MO1vN"/>

This page sorts them so each decision on the [[[[Supabase]] Warnings]] page can point to a reason. ‹9it2MD2rD›
  - Scope: the 10 errors, the 54 security-definer function warnings and the 4 repeated-auth-check warnings. The other warnings and the informational notices are not covered here. ‹v1lNKiUcn›
  - Background ‹NnwVHWM8d›
    - Row-level security (RLS) is how Postgres decides which rows each user can read or write. Each table has policies, and Postgres checks them for every row a query touches. ‹HS-ADpXMA›
    - Our policies call helper functions such as `my_space_ids('reader')` ("which spaces can the current user access?"). These helpers are `SECURITY DEFINER`: they run with the database owner's rights, so they can read the access tables, which users can't read directly. ‹fHOTihzKr›
    - Supabase has two roles that matter here. `anon` is any request made with the public API key and no login. `authenticated` is any logged-in request. Our plugins log in as a space's "anonymous" account, which uses the `authenticated` role, not `anon`. ‹wBiEWDIsU›
    - Supabase's advisor checks shapes, not behaviour. It flags any view that bypasses RLS, any view that reads `auth.users`, and any `SECURITY DEFINER` function that a role can execute. It can't tell whether the function or view leaks anything. ‹tuQTfUqya›
  - 1. Findings that stay ‹tdD-ESJvb›
    - `my_groups` reads `auth.users` (2 errors: ((dI7SeSOwP)) and ((3e4nCiOPH))) ‹9fxx9mOK-›
      - Groups are rows in Supabase's `auth.users` table, with a made-up email `{group name}@groups.discoursegraphs.com` (set by the `create-group` function). Group management needs to show users the groups they belong to. ‹BglrYKtOs›
      - The view returns only each group's id and name (the part of the email before the `@`), and only for groups the current user is a member of. A request without a login gets no rows. ‹hFV3C9RTW›
      - It has to run with the owner's rights, because users can't read `auth.users` themselves. So both findings stay. Background: ENG-1284. ‹-fITlDZK-›
    - Functions that stay executable (21 function warnings after the security batch) ‹gyAe5u12c›
      - The 21 are: 9 policy helpers and `upsert_account_in_space` for `authenticated`, 7 functions that the plugins and website call directly for `authenticated`, and 4 functions for `anon`. ‹z3fTaCoir›
      - The 7 called directly add accounts to a space, check whether a file was already uploaded, create and redeem tokens, accept group invitations, and list the caller's own accounts. Logged-in clients need them. The functions that add accounts get an access check first (section 3). ‹YNQK-4EVf›
      - Postgres requires the role making a query to have EXECUTE on every function its policies call. If we revoke a helper from a role, that role's queries on the table fail with a permission error. So every policy helper must stay executable by `authenticated`. ‹0gzgKtI0D›
      - The helpers are safe to call directly because they answer about the current user: "which spaces can I access?", "am I in this group?", "can I read this resource?". A direct call tells the caller nothing they couldn't learn by querying the table. ‹S09P2Z4SC›

      - We will later want to show some author details on public nodes to visitors, so that author information becomes public only when its owner decides. How that works belongs with [[Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts]]. Until then, public readers see `anonymous #<id>` for authors. ‹ayYZNwhGi›
  - 2. Security-definer views we keep for now: 8 errors, most of them for speed ‹YOKc48ben›
    - **Why it matters:** these 8 errors come from views that apply our access rules themselves, instead of letting RLS do it. We tested replacing them with RLS, and most got slower, one of them by about 2,700 times. So most of these errors stay, and we accept that. See the timings on ENG-2444. ‹MSLzXF5Cf›
    - Views: `my_accounts`, `my_spaces`, `my_concepts`, `my_contents`, `my_documents`, `my_file_references`, `my_contents_with_embedding_openai_text_embedding_3_small_1536`, `my_pseudo_accounts`. ‹5KzD-hhLg›
    - Why they exist: our policies called a helper like `in_space` for every row. On large reads, such as a sync or a listing, that cost caused timeouts (ENG-1433, ENG-1435, ENG-950). The views compute the user's accessible spaces once per query and filter on that, bypassing RLS. On a local database, a direct read of `Concept` took 114.5 ms; the same read through `my_concepts` took 2.5 ms. ‹LP4PN7
    - What Supabase objects to: a view that bypasses RLS holds a second copy of the access rules, and the two copies can drift apart. Single-table views were also writable, so writes through them skipped RLS. ENG-2368 and ENG-2359 closed that by revoking writes on the views. ‹QZN05PpFt›

ENG-2443 does this for
    - What we measured, with synthetic data at production's 273 `ResourceAccess` rows (ENG-2444): ‹M_EE2aFUn›

    - Broad default grants (25 of the 54 function warnings) ‹_-GBFZWoG›
      - `base.sql` granted every new function in the `public` schema to `anon` and `authenticated` by default. Many functions never needed that. ‹PHY_rlxYX›

    - Repeated auth checks (4 performance warnings) ‹o3GyNqgjM›

      - These are not advisor findings, but they come from the same functions. They are listed with the other security issue candidates in the October 8 sync notes: ((b8vNGrME7)). ‹eiwraOp96›

    - Repeated auth checks: 4 now. 0 after the fix. ‹PH0PAdQjA›

    - `security_model.md` is part of ENG-2442: `packages/database/doc/security_model.md`, on branch `eng-2442-grant-database-functions-only-to-the-roles-that-call-them`. That branch isn't pushed yet, because it waits for the rest of the security batch. ‹5nuk-v371›

    - [ENG-2442: Grant database functions only to the roles that call them​](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2442/grant-database-functions-only-to-the-roles-that-call-them) ‹XPoCbpLJ9›
    - Need / Problem Statement ‹JmWO5K2jp›
      - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? ‹PKPhmY5iN›
        - The problem is: every function in our `public` schema can be executed by `anon` (requests without a login) and by `authenticated` (logged-in requests), whether a client needs it or not. 25 of Supabase's 54 security-definer function warnings are grants that no client uses. ‹hynpWrGgr›

      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. Only deleting an account would use this index, and that is rare. Revisit if account deletion becomes routine. ‹CuCyRbOez›

      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **keep**. Only deleting an account would use this index, and that is rare. Revisit if account deletion becomes routine. ‹hYnhL4wlX›
  - **Unused indexes (3)** ‹hYAbwPomr›
    - `unused_index` · [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/database-linter?lint=0005_unused_index) ‹0KzUfBhiQ›
    - `public.Content`: [Content_text](…) ‹z_ci3PIR-›
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: keep. We're not using it now, but it will be used for database searches. ‹3l1frlPRh›
    - `public.access_token`: [access_token_code_idx](…) ‹w4eTFj1Uz›
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **fix**. ENG-2448 drops the unused table. ‹amfgKxmvH›
    - `public.access_token`: [access_token_platform_account_id_idx](…) ‹HhT-gv-lg›
      - Decision / reason / evidence:: **fix**. ENG-2448 drops the unused table. ‹ZQ_zOrgLs›
  - **Fixed Auth connection limit (1)** ‹OuYF7odQt›
    - [Auth is capped at 10 connections](…); the cap won't grow with instance size. `auth_db_connections_absolute` · [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/going-into-prod) ‹0_fn3On-d›
    - Decision / reason / evidence:: **fix**: switch the allocation strategy from Absolute to Percentage at 17%. On our instance (`max_connections` = 60) that is the same 10 connections, so nothing changes now, and the cap grows with the instance size. Peak use across all connections is currently 12. The Auth server only handles sign-ins, token refreshes and user management; logged-in data queries
- Why Supabase flags our database, and what we can change ‹MyX7CzumH›
  - **Why it matters:** Supabase's security advisor reports 10 errors and 54 function warnings on our database (snapshot of October 27, 2026). Some come from deliberate choices that stay. Some come from views that we keep, most of them for speed. The rest are mistakes that we can fix. This page sorts them so each decision on the [[[[Supabase]] Warnings]] page can point to a reason. ‹9it2MD2rD›
  - Scope: the 10 errors, the 54 security-definer function warnings and the 4 repeated-auth-check warnings. The other warnings and the informational notices are not covered here. ‹v1lNKiUcn›
  - Background ‹NnwVHWM8d›
    - Row-level security (RLS) is how Postgres decides which rows each user can read or write. Each table has policies, and Postgres checks them for every row a query touches. ‹HS-ADpXMA›
    - Our policies call helper functions such as `my_space_ids('reader')` ("which spaces can the current user access?"). These helpers are `SECURITY DEFINER`: they run with the database owner's rights, so they can read the access tables, which users can't read directly. ‹fHOTihzKr›
    - Supabase has two roles that matter here. `anon` is any request made with the public API key and no login. `authenticated` is any logged-in request. Our plugins log in as a space's "anonymous" account, which uses the `authenticated` role, not `anon`. ‹wBiEWDIsU›
    - Supabase's advisor checks shapes, not behaviour. It flags any view that bypasses RLS, any view that reads `auth.users`, and any `SECURITY DEFINER` function that a role can execute. It can't tell whether the function or view leaks anything. ‹tuQTfUqya›
  - 1. Findings that stay ‹tdD-ESJvb›
    - `my_groups` reads `auth.users` (2 errors: ((dI7SeSOwP)) and ((3e4nCiOPH))) ‹9fxx9mOK-›
      - Groups are rows in Supabase's `auth.users` table, with a made-up email `{group name}@groups.discoursegraphs.com` (set by the `create-group` function). Group management needs to show users the groups they belong to. ‹BglrYKtOs›
      - The view returns only each group's id and name (the part of the email before the `@`), and only for groups the current user is a member of. A request without a login gets no rows. ‹hFV3C9RTW›
      - It has to run with the owner's rights, because users can't read `auth.users` themselves. So both findings stay. Background: ENG-1284. ‹-fITlDZK-›
    - Functions that stay executable (21 function warnings after the security batch) ‹gyAe5u12c›
      - The 21 are: 9 policy helpers and `upsert_account_in_space` for `authenticated`, 7 functions that the plugins and website call directly for `authenticated`, and 4 functions for `anon`. ‹z3fTaCoir›
      - The 7 called directly add accounts to a space, check whether a file was already uploaded, create and redeem tokens, accept group invitations, and list the caller's own accounts. Logged-in clients need them. The functions that add accounts get an access check first (section 3). ‹YNQK-4EVf›
      - Postgres requires the role making a query to have EXECUTE on every function its policies call. If we revoke a helper from a role, that role's queries on the table fail with a permission error. So every policy helper must stay executable by `authenticated`. ‹0gzgKtI0D›
      - The helpers are safe to call directly because they answer about the current user: "which spaces can I access?", "am I in this group?", "can I read this resource?". A direct call tells the caller nothing they couldn't learn by querying the table. ‹S09P2Z4SC›
      - Some helpers must also stay executable by `anon`: ‹WG1w3NUmn›
        - Needed today: `my_space_ids`, because `anon` can query `Space`, whose select policy calls it. Also `get_secret_token`, which the website calls to hand a plugin's session to a browser that isn't logged in yet. That token is 12 random bytes, single use, and expires after 45 seconds. ‹rXlwYDJX_›
        - Needed for public nodes: `my_user_accounts`, `my_space_ids` and `file_access`. Visitors without a login will read public nodes and their files through these functions (ENG-1837 and the planned public account). Revoking them now would mean granting them back. ‹I_BUgWwN2›
      - We will later want to show some author details on public nodes to visitors, so that author information becomes public only when its owner decides. How that works belongs with [[Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts]]. Until then, public readers see `anonymous #<id>` for authors. ‹ayYZNwhGi›
  - 2. Security-definer views we keep for now: 8 errors, most of them for speed ‹YOKc48ben›
    - **Why it matters:** these 8 errors come from views that apply our access rules themselves, instead of letting RLS do it. We tested replacing them with RLS, and most got slower, one of them by about 2,700 times. So most of these errors stay, and we accept that. See the timings on ENG-2444. ‹MSLzXF5Cf›
    - Views: `my_accounts`, `my_spaces`, `my_concepts`, `my_contents`, `my_documents`, `my_file_references`, `my_contents_with_embedding_openai_text_embedding_3_small_1536`, `my_pseudo_accounts`. ‹5KzD-hhLg›
    - Why they exist: our policies called a helper like `in_space` for every row. On large reads, such as a sync or a listing, that cost caused timeouts (ENG-1433, ENG-1435, ENG-950). The views compute the user's accessible spaces once per query and filter on that, bypassing RLS. On a local database, a direct read of `Concept` took 114.5 ms; the same read through `my_concepts` took 2.5 ms. ‹LP4PN7
    - What Supabase objects to: a view that bypasses RLS holds a second copy of the access rules, and the two copies can drift apart. Single-table views were also writable, so writes through them skipped RLS. ENG-2368 and ENG-2359 closed that by revoking writes on the views. ‹QZN05PpFt›
    - What we now know: per-row helper calls were a large part of the cost. Postgres doesn't reuse a function's result from one row to the next, so a helper in a filter runs once per row. Wrapping a call that doesn't depend on the row in `(SELECT ...)` makes Postgres compute it once per query. ENG-2344 used this inside `my_concepts` and cut a listing from 232.5 ms to 2.4 ms. ENG-2443 does this for
    - What we measured, with synthetic data at production's 273 `ResourceAccess` rows (ENG-2444): ‹M_EE2aFUn›
      - `concept_in_relations` goes from 10 ms to 2,500 ms for 100 nodes, through `security_invoker` views and through the tables. Its filter uses `@>`, which isn't `LEAKPROOF`, so under RLS the policy has to run first and the `refs` index can't be used. ‹VGz7hgcDO›
      - `getConcepts` with content goes from 7 ms to about 100 ms. We haven't found out why. ‹LIAvbGAVG›
      - Listings get 20-90% slower, over the ticket's 25% limit. ‹8JIdSFkws›
      - Gains only appear around 100 times today's `ResourceAccess` size. ‹cW6dj3Qjq›
      - The tables aren't a way around this. They go through the same RLS, and some embeds only exist for the views (ENG-2445). ‹Q8cwv_cdp›
    - These views can't convert for reasons other than speed: `my_accounts` and `my_pseudo_accounts`, explained in their decisions under ((3e4nCiOPH)). ‹3SVpSlDIO›
  - 3. Mistakes that we can fix ‹BVN3V236T›
    - Broad default grants (25 of the 54 function warnings) ‹_-GBFZWoG›
      - `base.sql` granted every new function in the `public` schema to `anon` and `authenticated` by default. Many functions never needed that. ‹PHY_rlxYX›
      - Revoke from both roles (14 warnings): the six trigger functions, which only triggers call, and `is_last_local_reference`, which only those triggers call. Called directly, `is_last_local_reference` reveals whether a row exists in a space the caller can't read. ‹M2tnsrWZq›
      - Revoke from `anon` only (11 warnings): `create_account_in_space`, `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space`, `file_exists`, `create_secret_token`, `accept_group_invitation`, `generic_entity_access`, `in_group`, `is_group_admin`, `group_exists`, `in_space`. None is called without a login. `generic_entity_access` loses `anon` together with `anon`'s grants on `sync_info`. ‹IscYwDs
      - ENG-2442 changes the default, so a new function gets no `anon` grant unless we add one on purpose. ‹btA6KselW›
    - Repeated auth checks (4 performance warnings) ‹o3GyNqgjM›
      - The `group_membership` delete policy and three `secret_token` policies call `auth.uid()` directly. Writing `(SELECT auth.uid())` makes Postgres evaluate it once per query. ‹Zwp16j5J-›
    - Security holes found during this review ‹YD8Rv3yjp›
      - These are not advisor findings, but they come from the same functions. They are listed with the other security issue candidates in the October 8 sync notes: ((b8vNGrME7)). ‹eiwraOp96›
        - `upsert_account_in_space` doesn't check that the caller can access the space. A logged-in user can give themselves editor access to another space. Issue candidate: ((5cTXWhzAt)) ‹04t-Q122y›
        - `group_exists` and the `group_membership` insert policy let a user claim a uuid that isn't yet a group. Issue candidate: ((Wwm8OO2uF)) ‹WaM9GTju-›
  - Expected counts ‹y8hgGIgD_›
    - Errors: 10 now. 11 after the security batch: 2 on `my_groups`, the other 8 `my_*` views, and `accounts_in_my_partial_spaces`, which ENG-2446 adds. ‹Ph1Ne7z4Q›
    - Security-definer function warnings: 54 now. 21 after the security batch: 4 for `anon` and 17 for `authenticated`. ‹ppHxEIHZF›
    - Repeated auth checks: 4 now. 0 after the fix. ‹PH0PAdQjA›
  - Next steps ‹7b0JKivaN›
    - The revokes and the auth-check fix. No behaviour change is expected; the test suite should confirm that. Issue candidate: ((5CHcLj89v)) ‹6XoNlui99›
    - The RLS rewrite, with the tests above (ENG-2443). The `security_invoker` views are parked (ENG-2444), and the plugins stay on the views (ENG-2445). Issue candidate: ((EGL5PRVvc)) ‹SRypOhGdQ›
    - The `upsert_account_in_space` fix: ((5cTXWhzAt)) ‹Wq7l5IWMt›
    - `security_model.md` is part of ENG-2442: `packages/database/doc/security_model.md`, on branch `eng-2442-grant-database-functions-only-to-the-roles-that-call-them`. That branch isn't pushed yet, because it waits for the rest of the security batch. ‹5nuk-v371›
- Issue candidates ‹bSdA0PVz7›
  - Grant database functions only to the roles that call them ‹5CHcLj89v›
    - [ENG-2442: Grant database functions only to the roles that call them​](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2442/grant-database-functions-only-to-the-roles-that-call-them) ‹XPoCbpLJ9›
    - Need / Problem Statement ‹JmWO5K2jp›
      - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? ‹PKPhmY5iN›
        - The problem is: every function in our `public` schema can be executed by `anon` (requests without a login) and by `authenticated` (logged-in requests), whether a client needs it or not. 25 of Supabase's 54 security-definer function warnings are grants that no client uses. ‹hynpWrGgr›
        - Cause: `base.sql` sets default privileges that grant every new function in `public` to `anon` and `authenticated`. Nobody chose these grants function by function. ‹i3lEpOHIw›
        - An unused grant lets anyone call a `SECURITY DEFINER` function directly, outside the flow it was written for. Such a function runs with the owner's rights and skips row-level security. ((5cTXWhzAt)) shows what one direct call can do. ‹cynJuBWzI›
        - Also in scope: four policies call `auth.uid()` once per row instead of once per query (Supabase's repeated-auth-check warnings). ‹d8h3xi3dj›
        - Background and reasons: ((_-GBFZWoG)) and ((o3GyNqgjM)). ‹ZTCTM16sI›
      - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them? ‹ybl_cht1G›

# Environment update
 - Primary working directory: /Users/maparent/OpenSource/discourse-graph (was /Users/maparent/OpenSource/discourse-graph/packages/database/supabase)

Your counts are right: 11 errors and 23 warnings, with 20 function warnings (4 for `anon` and 16 for `authenticated`), all matching your CSV export. The two lists of fixed functions and the two new function entries have mistakes, though. I read lines 1 to 320 of the page's 613: the Errors, Warnings, Informational notices and "Why Supabase flags our database" sections. I skipped the issue-candidate drafts after that. I haven't written anything to Roam.

## Mistakes

1. **The `anon` "Removed from" list is wrong** (under "27->4"). It lists the four functions that remain (`file_access`, `get_secret_token`, `my_space_ids`, `my_user_accounts`). It also lists `account_ids_in_shared_spaces` and `my_platform_account_ids`, which are new in the batch and were never granted to `anon`. It's missing 12 of the 23 that were actually removed. The correct 23 are:
   - `accept_group_invitation`, `account_in_shared_space`, `after_delete_space`, `after_delete_update_fref`, `after_insert_fref`
   - `can_access_account`, `can_view_specific_resource`, `create_account_in_space`, `create_secret_token`, `file_exists`
   - `generic_entity_access`, `group_exists`, `in_group`, `in_space`, `is_group_admin`
   - `is_last_local_reference`, `is_my_account`, `on_delete_local_reference`, `on_delete_space_revoke_local_access`, `on_update_local_reference`
   - `unowned_account_in_shared_space`, `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space`
2. **The `authenticated` "Solved" list has only 3 of the 13** it should have. 27 − 13 + 2 new = 16. The 13 are:
   - the six trigger functions
   - `is_last_local_reference`
   - `account_in_shared_space`, `can_access_account`, `can_view_specific_resource`, `group_exists`, `is_my_account`, `unowned_account_in_shared_space`
3. **The `account_ids_in_shared_space(p_account_id bigint, …)` entry has the wrong name and signature.** The function is `account_ids_in_shared_spaces(access_level public."SpaceAccessPermissions")`, with an "s" and no account argument.
4. **The `my_platform_account_ids(access_level …)` entry has the wrong signature.** The function takes no arguments: `my_platform_account_ids()`. The advisor's id for it ends in `_my_platform_account_ids_`, with nothing after the name.
5. **`group_exists` still says "authenticated: **keep** for now".** ENG-2438 dropped the function (migration `20261101130000`), so it should read like the other removed functions: "**fix**: removed by ENG-2438".
6. **`can_view_concept` and `can_view_content` were never advisor findings.** They aren't `SECURITY DEFINER`, so they weren't among the 27. ENG-2443 did drop them, so either delete them from the list or say "not an advisor finding".
7. **Some counts are stale:**
   - The top **Errors (10)** header should be 10->11.
   - In the "Why Supabase flags our database" section, both "Functions that stay executable (21 …)" and "Expected counts" still say 21, with 17 for `authenticated`. The real counts are 20 and 16, because `group_exists` is gone.
   - The breakdown should now read: 9 policy helpers plus `upsert_account_in_space`, 6 functions called directly, and 4 for `anon`. The "7 called directly" description also covers listing the caller's own accounts; no function on the current list does that.

## Format

- **The two new function entries** lack the links line and the `Decision::` / `Reason / evidence::` pair. Suggested text:
  - `account_ids_in_shared_spaces(access_level public."SpaceAccessPermissions")`
    - [authenticated](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=WARN&id=authenticated_security_definer_function_executable_public_account_ids_in_shared_spaces_access_level%20public.%22SpaceAccessPermissions%22)
    - Decision:: authenticated: **keep**
    - Reason / evidence:: Account write policies call it once per query, in place of `account_in_shared_space` and `unowned_account_in_shared_space`, which ran once per row. Added by ENG-2446. Never granted to `anon`.
  - `my_platform_account_ids()`
    - [authenticated](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz/advisors/security?preset=WARN&id=authenticated_security_definer_function_executable_public_my_platform_account_ids_)
    - Decision:: authenticated: **keep**
    - Reason / evidence:: Returns the caller's own platform account ids. Policies call it once per query, in place of `is_my_account`, which ran once per row. Added by ENG-2443. Never granted to `anon`.

  I'm assuming you build the links the same way as for the existing entries. Check that they open before you paste them.
- **The `accounts_in_my_partial_spaces` decision** could say which PR added the view and drop the capitalised "BUT". For example: "**keep**. ENG-2446 added it so account policies check access once per query. It could move out of the schema PostgREST exposes: ((QMPLUito7))".
- **There's an empty block** (`WQF5v59cC`) at the end of "Function removed".
- **Several decisions still use the future tense.** The remaining revoke entries say "**fix** (revoke) … Tracked in ((5CHcLj89v))", the "Access restricted" entries do the same, and so do the four repeated-auth-check entries. All of these are done now, in ENG-2442's migration `20261030180000`. Adding "done by ENG-2442" would match how you wrote the removed functions. This one is optional.
- **Some decision keywords aren't bold:** "fix." on `pg_stat_monitor`, "Investigate." on OTP expiry, and "keep." on `Content_text`.

I can write these changes to the page if you'd like, but only once you say so.

{"guidelines":"# roam/agent guidelines <roam uid="XcDxM3AGm" refs="11"/>

- This is the **discourse-graphs team graph** (dg-team). It tracks product development, user research, and design knowledge for the Discourse Graphs project. Start orientation at [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]]. <roam uid="ZyEFQdPzy"/>
- Graph Ontology <roam uid="CkMv_I9Hu" heading="2"/>
  - This graph uses a discourse graph node grammar with typed nodes. Each node type has a title format that the Roam plugin uses for identification via regex. Nodes exist at two levels of formality: <roam uid="JZ-ERybz9"/>
    - **Full node pages** — titled with the type prefix (e.g., `[[ISS]] - description`). These are the primary knowledge units. <roam uid="Lr2QOC061"/>
    - **Candidate nodes** — blocks tagged with a candidate hashtag (e.g., `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`). These are seedling ideas not yet promoted to full pages. <roam uid="IxTd36BlH"/>
  - Node Types: Knowledge <roam uid="iJARoph1H" heading="3"/>
    - **Question (QUE)** — the unknowns being explored through pilots and research. Format: `[[QUE]] - {content}`. Sections: Summary, Notes, Testable hypotheses, Snippets. <roam uid="9uXF_YcQQ"/>
    - **Hypothesis (HYP)** — proposed answers to questions; collect evidence for or against. Format: `[[HYP]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#hyp-candidate`. Sections: Rationale, Snippets, Requests for Experiments. <roam uid="jA0VLkwMY"/>
    - **Result (RES)** — a discrete observation from ongoing research, in past tense. Format: `[[RES]] - {content} - {Source}`. Candidate tag: `#res-candidate`. Sections: Summary, Grounding Context, Snippets. Properties: NodeFormality (Draft → ReadyForInternal → ReadyToShare → Published), Contributors. <roam uid="21s0GTu6p"/>
    - **Evidence (EVD)** — a discrete observation from a published dataset or experiment. Format: `[[EVD]] - {content} - {Source}`. Sections: Evidence Description, Snippets, Grounding Context, Centrality slider. <roam uid="zgYL5nVb4"/>
    - **Claim (CLM)** — an assertion about how discourse graphs work or should work. Format: `[[CLM]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#clm-candidate`. <roam uid="9SOQK_533"/>
    - **Source (SRC)** — a referenced publication or external resource. Format: `@{content}`. <roam uid="wenbahwqN"/>
    - **Theory (THE)** — a theoretical framework or model. Format: `[[THE]] - {content}`. <roam uid="UtoPH2BxJ"/>
  - Node Types: Product & UX <roam uid="e-gV24nNQ" heading="3"/>
    - **Function (FUN)** — a UX "use case": a specific situation where Discourse Graphs can be used to enhance the experience. Tool-agnostic in framing, but tied to a concrete user goal. Format: `[[FUN]] - {content}`. Properties: FunctionImportance, FunctionScoping. <roam uid="LjYlqRpUR"/>
    - **Flow (FLO)** — a set of interactions the user performs to accomplish a goal within a particular implementation of Discourse Graphs (Obsidian plugin, Roam plugin, tldraw, etc.). A Flow is the tool-specific instantiation of a Function/Use Case. Format: `[[FLO]] - {content}`. Sections: Description (Goal, Loom, brief description), Steps (Normal flow, Alt flows, Exceptions), Examples, Pain points. Properties: FlowStatus (💭 Hypothetical → 🗓️ Planned → 🤔 Experimental → 🚧 Bespoke → 🔨 Alpha → 🚀 Beta), FlowFrequency, FlowImpact. <roam uid="SVcbz9E3i"/>
    - **Artifact (ART)** — the features, workflows, and UI components we build to enable Flows and Use Cases (Functions). Parts of a system are prefixed with the system name (e.g., `[[ART]] - Roam DG/Query`). Format: `[[ART]] - {content}`. Properties: ArtifactType (Feature/Component or Workflow/Template), ArtStatus (🤔 Prospective → 🖇️ Bespoke → 🧪 Alpha → 🎯 Beta → 💎 Release → 🌐 External). <roam uid="71FJwPgwi"/>
    - **PainPoint (PAI)** — problems, friction, and bottlenecks in user experience. Format: `[[PAI]] - {content}`. Properties: Activity, Function, Flow, UserTool. <roam uid="zD3lBBh9A"/>
    - **Journey (JOU)** — a user journey across multiple functions/flows. Format: `[[JOU]] - {content}`. Sections: Description, Phases, Pain points, Notes. <roam uid="YmhUG6VJX"/>
    - **Activity (ACT)** — an action the user performs that is not specific to any particular tool or method (e.g., "synthesize literature," "discuss findings"). Activities sit upstream of tool-bound Flows and Use Cases. Format: `[[ACT]] - {content}`. <roam uid="1NcVa1g2X"/>
    - **UserPilot** — a specific user or pilot engagement. Format: `UserPilot/{content}`. Properties: User status, UserTool (Roam, Obsidian, Notion, tldraw), UserType (Alpha/Beta/Normie), Lead. <roam uid="5XUZyDshG"/>
    - **CaseStudy (CAS)** — a documented case study. Format: `[[CAS]] - {content}`. <roam uid="ceCyzY2Ei"/>
  - Node Types: Project Management <roam uid="L4Lo_4B1w" heading="3"/>
    - **Issue (ISS)** — a potential action item for development or research. Format: `[[ISS]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#iss-candidate`. Properties: Issue Status (🤔 Considering → 🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → 💬 Awaiting Feedback → ➡ Sent To Linear → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Issue Type (🗳️ Feature Request, 📄 Template improvement, 🐞 Bug Report, 🔬 Research, 🏗️ DG team, 🛠️ Maintenance), Priority, Project, Function, Flow, Lead. <roam uid="jzczOjTM1"/>
    - **Project** — a research or development project. Format: `Project/{content}`. Properties: Project Status (🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Priority. <roam uid="IwUFa4By7"/>
    - **Milestone** — a time-boxed delivery target. Format: `Milestone/{content}`. Properties: Milestone Status, Start/End Date, Priority. <roam uid="NCfJPwcoO"/>
  - Relation Types <roam uid="PZxB_Lim1" heading="3"/>
    - **Supports / Supported By** — Evidence or Result supports a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="QLrw6Cikm"/>
    - **Opposes / Opposed By** — Evidence or Result contradicts a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="RdGHvBjvu"/>
    - **Informs / Informed By** — Evidence, Result, or Claim informs a Question or Hypothesis; Question informs Hypothesis; Hypothesis informs Issue <roam uid="0TFxQSHzV"/>
    - **Reproduces / Reproduced By** — Evidence confirms other Evidence <roam uid="lZNpV65LF"/>
    - **Resolves / Is resolved by** — Result resolves an Issue <roam uid="BKCUPTVYB"/>
    - To query typed relations programmatically, use `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…` (the `discourse` MCP) — it returns a node's Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves edges and their complements directly. See **Which MCP tool for which task** under Navigating. The `roam` MCP can't resolve typed relations; with it, fall back to following page references within node content and checking linked references. <roam uid="4uQA80UCZ"/>
- Navigating the Graph <roam uid="I5GtkN5Cn" heading="2"/>
  - Which MCP tool for which task <roam uid="0w3wW5Rny" heading="3"/>
    - Two MCP servers read this graph. Reach for the **`discourse`** server whenever a task depends on the discourse-node / relation grammar (typed nodes, typed relations, the ontology); use the **`roam`** server for general text search, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes. <roam uid="v7YWcac84"/>
    - **Find discourse nodes by topic** → `mcp__discourse__search_nodes` (all query words must appear in the node title; optional `node_type_format` regex restricts to one type, e.g. `\[\[FLO\]\]` for Flows). For free-text across __all__ blocks — meeting notes, daily notes, non-node content — use `mcp__roam__search` instead. <roam uid="OmYGreM1F"/>
    - **List every node of a type** (all Flows, all Issues, …) → `mcp__discourse__get_all_discourse_nodes` (optional `since` ISO date for "what's new"). More reliable than a roam prefix search, which can miss nodes. <roam uid="OMwgWxWHS"/>
    - **Read a node's full content** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` for the title + full block tree; `mcp__roam__get_page` / `mcp__roam__get_block` are the general-purpose equivalents. <roam uid="2LarSnz-g"/>
    - **Find a node's typed relations** (what Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves it) → `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…`. Resolves the typed edges directly; the roam server cannot. <roam uid="GS3OMHszL"/>
    - **Walk a node's neighborhood** (multi-hop reference graph) → `mcp__discourse__get_node_neighborhood uid=… depth=1–4 direction=both`. <roam uid="ur9V-QLL7"/>
    - **Get the live ontology** (node types + relation definitions) → `mcp__discourse__get_discourse_node_types`. The source of truth behind the **Graph Ontology** section above — pull it when you suspect the documented types or relations have drifted. <roam uid="qVG4hiqaO"/>
    - **General text search, recency, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes** → the **`roam`** server: `mcp__roam__search` (empty query = recently edited / viewed), `get_page`, `get_block`, `get_backlinks`, `create_block`, `update_block`. The `discourse` server is read-only. <roam uid="Tf4JXJyRu"/>
    - **Read the publication behind an `@source`** → check its `metadata::` / `Abstract::` block first; for full text use the `zotero` MCP (`mcp__zotero__*`) when it's in the user's Zotero library. <roam uid="wsMfcY8Rf"/>
    - **Find who created a block** → `mcp__roam__datalog_query` on `:create/user`. There is no dedicated block-author tool on either MCP server; this query is the only reliable way to get block-level provenance. Always bind it to a page or a uid — unbounded, it returns every block in the graph. <roam uid="YemilM2pX" refs="1"/>
      - By page: `[:find ?uid ?creator ?editor :in $ ?page-title :where [?p :node/title ?page-title] [?b :block/page ?p] [?b :block/uid ?uid] [?b :create/user ?cu] [?cu :user/display-page ?cp] [?cp :node/title ?creator] [?b :edit/user ?eu] [?eu :user/display-page ?ep] [?ep :node/title ?editor]]` — returns uid + names only. Don't add `?b :block/string ?s` unless you need it: it re-returns the whole page you already read, roughly 7x the tokens. <roam uid="7BKClr9BK" refs="1"/>
      - For a single block, replace the two page clauses with `[?b :block/uid ?uid]` and pass the uid as the input. <roam uid="icLRn-ci0" refs="1"/>
    - **Find who created a page or discourse node** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` returns `author`, `author_uid`, `created`, `modified`. Page-level only — given a __block__ uid it returns the content with no author, so fall back to the datalog query above. <roam uid="wRmrVnFqO" refs="1"/>
    - **List every identity in the graph** → `mcp__discourse__get_users` — humans, bots, and API tokens with their uids. Resolve a partial name here before making any authorship claim. <roam uid="7IXa9Yq2g" refs="1"/>
    - **See what one person wrote recently** → `mcp__discourse__catch_me_up author="…" days=N`. Needs the exact display name from `get_users`. <roam uid="0gEBMNuKz" refs="1"/>
    - **Find the discourse nodes a person authored** → `mcp__discourse__get_researcher_contributions author="…"`. Node __pages__ only — it returns 0 for identities that write blocks but never create node pages, so a 0 is not evidence that someone wrote nothing. <roam uid="0OshhlAu4" refs="1"/>
    - **Filter an existing query by author** → `mcp__discourse__run_discourse_query query_uid=…` honors the query builder's `created by` / `edited by` conditions. <roam uid="MyIALn-lG" refs="1"/>
    - On every call, pass the graph explicitly (`graph="dg-team"`) — several graphs are configured, and the wrong one silently returns nothing. <roam uid="STWu7JWy_"/>
  - Entry point <roam uid="MHzuk97bt" heading="3"/>
    - Start from [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]], which orients you to the main dashboards, functions/flows, pilot status, and hypotheses/results. <roam uid="nPt2-iVnj"/>
  - Following page references for context <roam uid="h9NTRhMjK" heading="3"/>
    - Much of a node's meaning lives in its **page references** — the `[[double-bracketed]]` links within its content blocks. These connect nodes to the Functions, Flows, Projects, Sources, and UserPilots that give them context. <roam uid="U28zLlsXL"/>
    - When reading a node, expand or follow its page references to understand **why** it exists and **what** it connects to. For example, a Result node's title includes its Source (e.g., `[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]`), and its body may reference the Function or Flow it relates to. <roam uid="BQMJ8e_-z"/>
    - **Linked references** (at the bottom of any page) show every block in the graph that mentions that page. This is the primary way to see how a node is used in context — meeting notes, update logs, other discourse nodes, and daily notes entries. <roam uid="G9z0oYOKm"/>
    - **Block references** work similarly for individual blocks (bullets). If a block has a reference count, it has been cited elsewhere. <roam uid="Dcv_AHP0W"/>
  - Search strategies <roam uid="uDgL2s89Q" heading="3"/>
    - Search for discourse nodes by their type prefix: `[[QUE]] -`, `[[ISS]] -`, `[[FLO]] -`, `[[RES]] -`, etc. <roam uid="z9FqVtbYA"/>
    - Search for candidate nodes by their tag: `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate`. <roam uid="R6ZQgo7E-"/>
    - Search with empty query to see recently edited and viewed content — useful for understanding current activity. <roam uid="aHXgbk2iE"/>
    - For attributes with constrained values (status fields, priorities, tools, etc.), refer to [[roam/js/attribute-select]] for the canonical set of options. <roam uid="MaJPh5WXZ"/>
  - Understanding overall workflows <roam uid="3Qe0kZwzj" heading="3"/>
    - An observation from a pilot (Result) often triggers an idea for improvement (Issue). Issues are higher priority when they improve an important Flow, which in turn enables a key Function. Once engineering works on an issue, it becomes a feature (Artifact). <roam uid="E-6z55uoF"/>
    - Result → Issue → Flow → Function → Artifact traces the path from observation to shipped feature. <roam uid="gFNP0A0S9"/>
- Writing into the graph <roam uid="a7uWA6zlm" heading="2"/>
  - Leave node creation and tagging to the team by default (see **Agent Behavior → General rules** below). When you are explicitly asked to capture something — a candidate node, a pilot observation, a flow — follow these conventions so each block reads cleanly now **and** is trivial to promote into a formal discourse node later. <roam uid="mebOIP95I"/>
  - Put each concept in its own block <roam uid="F3EVfNmD7" heading="3"/>
    - Write one idea — one claim, observation, pain point, flow, or action — per block. Don't pack several into a single bullet. Be parsimonious with any commentary you consider adding. <roam uid="1LMq1Ui6Y"/>
      - Atomic blocks are individually addressable: each can be block-referenced (`((uid))`), tagged, and promoted to a node on its own. A compound bullet can't. <roam uid="rLZacptHP"/>
    - Use indentation to carry structure: the parent block states the idea; child blocks hold its detail, caveats, steps, and references. <roam uid="VFcltIeP4"/>
      - This mirrors a discourse node, where the title is the idea and the template sections are the children. <roam uid="dv7_tHNg5"/>
  - Make candidate blocks formalizable <roam uid="t62zcsYxS" heading="3"/>
    - When you tag a block with a candidate tag, write the statement so it can become the node's **title almost verbatim** — the eventual node title should be roughly the same words as the block. Keep it atomic and self-contained: understandable without the surrounding meeting / log context. <roam uid="QcHWU8FCu"/>
    - Match the target node's title grammar so promotion is mechanical. The candidate tags in use here are `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate` — each maps to the node type of the same prefix (see **Graph Ontology** above for every format). Common cases: <roam uid="vNFJ3JbII"/>
      - `#res-candidate` → a discrete, past-tense pilot observation → `[[RES]] - {statement} - {Source}`. Name the `@source` / UserPilot in a child so it can be appended to the title on promotion. <roam uid="Xx5QnpXMw"/>
        - Example: `Pilot users created 3x more claims after the canvas node preview shipped #res-candidate` <roam uid="8RsFzOBwL"/>
      - `#iss-candidate` → an actionable dev or research item → `[[ISS]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="0tM9FtTCr"/>
        - Example: `Group nodes on the canvas by semantic similarity #iss-candidate` <roam uid="b8CJepmiH"/>
      - `#flow-candidate` → a tool-specific interaction flow → `[[FLO]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="alG4QCDR4"/>
        - Example: `Preview / view DG node info while on the tldraw canvas #flow-candidate` <roam uid="skG-2mzeZ"/>
    - If you can't yet phrase an idea atomically, leave it as plain text and don't tag it — a vague stub can't be promoted without a rewrite. <roam uid="znTpKgzZv"/>
  - Put supporting context in child blocks <roam uid="YE6FUcUKB" heading="3"/>
    - Everything that explains, grounds, or qualifies a candidate goes in **child blocks beneath it, never crammed into the statement**.  On promotion these children carry over into the node's template sections. <roam uid="VwHNAB0ij"/>
    - `#res-candidate` → Source + method + a screenshot or Loom → **Grounding Context** and **Snippets**. `#flow-candidate` → **Description** (Goal, Loom), **Steps**, **Pain points**. `#iss-candidate` → why it matters + the Flow / Function it improves → Issue Status / Type / Project / Flow properties. <roam uid="-zzjS0GNH"/>
    - Link related nodes with `[[…]]` inside the children — those page references become the node's discourse connections (Supports / Opposes / Informs / Resolves) once it is formalized. <roam uid="pM5ojIoXO"/>
  - Reuse the existing syntax and formatting conventions <roam uid="MEWdJCUaQ" heading="3"/>
    - For how to __reference__ nodes when writing (Roam alias syntax, `((uid))`), follow **Agent Behavior → Citing and referencing nodes** below — don't paste full URLs inside Roam. <roam uid="iqnB7VJ1X"/>
    - For callouts, colors, and foldable blocks, use the palette documented in **Agent Behavior → Formatting** below. <roam uid="1-PwVXvKX"/>
    - Reference only node titles you have actually found in the graph; never fabricate one. Preserve node title regex formats exactly (`[[RES]] - … - {Source}`, `[[FLO]] - …`, `UserPilot/…`) — a malformed title silently drops the block out of the discourse graph. <roam uid="ldsx0Q1Nj"/>
- Agent Behavior <roam uid="HQkVaTtF9" heading="2"/>
  - Information hierarchy <roam uid="Omx-xxku_" heading="3"/>
    - **Prioritize formalized node pages** (full `[[TYPE]] - title` pages with templates filled in). These represent the team's vetted, structured knowledge. <roam uid="gSd5Imn_Z"/>
    - **Then candidate nodes** (`#type-candidate` tagged blocks). These are preliminary but intentionally captured ideas. <roam uid="KPWTNgy6Z"/>
    - **Then remaining content** (meeting notes, daily notes, log entries, comments). These provide context but are less curated. <roam uid="7FBUcDopw"/>
    - Rank by formality, but check authorship before you cite — only human-written blocks are citable. See **Synthesize human content, not agent content** below. <roam uid="RgZPUYxXj" refs="1"/>
  - Synthesize human content, not agent content <roam uid="IxsMpHOOT" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Your job is synthesis of what the team's people wrote.**  Building on agent-authored content closes a loop where agents cite agents and the graph fills with its own echo. <roam uid="2vCRnvaM-" refs="1"/>
    - **This includes your own prior output.** Never cite, quote, count, or treat as evidence a block that you or another agent wrote, in this graph or any other. <roam uid="r-7VcjnUB" refs="1"/>
  - Provenance: who wrote this block <roam uid="psNqP1Ow4" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Never ascribe a statement to a person without querying the block's creator.** Position in the outline, a nearby name, and a `#[[Name]]` tag are not authorship signals — a person tag usually marks an assignee or a mention, and meeting notes are typed by one scribe on everyone's behalf. Look up `:create/user` before writing "X thinks", "per Joel", or any attributed quote. <roam uid="QowkWQTjg" refs="1"/>
    - **When creator and last editor differ, report both.** "Created by `matt-AI-bot`, last edited by Karola Kirsanow" is the honest form. Don't collapse it to one name. <roam uid="ABeXcABpE" refs="1"/>
    - **Speaker initials in meeting notes are the exception, and you should honor them.** On `Sync /` pages, `JC:`, `MAP:`, `MG:`, `KK:`, `MA:` are the scribe's record of who spoke. Attribute the __position__ to the initials and the __block__ to its creator, and say the initials are your basis. <roam uid="zgFhSiYI6" refs="1"/>
    - **If you can't resolve authorship, say the block is unattributed.** Never assign it to the nearest name on the page. <roam uid="CFgMF_i0-" refs="1"/>
    - **Non-human identities in this graph today:** `matt-AI-bot`, `ai-cybrarian`, `cybrarian-ai`, `Michael Gartner (AI)`, and every identity whose display name begins with `API Token:` or `Local API Token:`. Treat those as machine-written unless you have checked otherwise. Per-bot users are still being sorted out — see [[Convention/Human-AI interaction in Roam]]. <roam uid="78YnS6gEC" refs="1"/>
      - A token is not automatically an agent. `API Token: Raycast matt` and `API Token: send2graph` forward text a human typed. Token-created means __provenance unclear__, not __AI-generated__ — report which one you actually found. <roam uid="VBVOklCV1" refs="1"/>
      - `Discourse Graphs`, `Anonymous`, and `Anonymous_1`–`Anonymous_3` are shared or unresolved accounts. Don't attribute their blocks to any individual. <roam uid="rHnvdFRhH" refs="1"/>
    - **You may read agent content as context, but don't cite it.** Use an agent-written summary or digest to locate the human blocks underneath, then read and cite those. Consider the agent-written content as background context, not citable material. <roam uid="tCRWvyruf" refs="1"/>
    - **When the human record is thin, say so.** If the only coverage of a topic is agent-written, report that the team has not covered it rather than laundering an agent's take into a finding. <roam uid="PDwgHjakx" refs="1"/>
  - Citing and referencing nodes <roam uid="1Q-QuB4hm" heading="3"/>
    - When referencing discourse nodes in your responses, use **Roam alias syntax** so the link is readable but navigable: <roam uid="iZecLmaRZ"/>
      - `[the claim about synthesis]([[[[CLM]] - discourse graphs improve synthesis]])` <roam uid="-XCMrdIIk"/>
      - `[this pilot result]([[[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]]]])` <roam uid="47VfBEfiy"/>
      - `[canvas node preview flow]([[[[FLO]] - Preview/view DG node info while on canvas]])` <roam uid="9VQN1PcbM"/>
      - `[the grouping issue]([[[[ISS]] - group nodes on the canvas, eg by semantic similarity]])` <roam uid="huKrbfYiZ"/>
    - For block-level references, use the `((uid))` syntax when you have a specific block UID. <roam uid="P03iIKmxK"/>
    - Always include enough of the node title for the reader to understand the reference without clicking through. <roam uid="6rl43A8ym"/>
  - Citing dates <roam uid="FNMHIgv1c" heading="3"/>
    - The team uses the linked references of daily notes pages as a "table of contents" to monitor the team's work that week. Therefore, be judicious in how many times you reference a daily note with wikilinks. The top-level entry usually includes a reference to today's date, and any clear deadline can be referenced once per entry. Other dates should be labeled like `July 29` rather than with wikilinks. <roam uid="AJ-MJrH7M"/>
  - Reading nodes thoroughly <roam uid="UJfOc9mSn" heading="3"/>
    - When investigating a node, don't stop at the title. Read the template sections (Summary, Description, Rationale, etc.) for substance, and follow page references in the content for context. <roam uid="9mWl4_KbG"/>
    - All the firebase links are public links to images.  Usually, these images are very informative, so for relevant nodes and pages you should open the images and interpret them with your image recognition capabilities <roam uid="EIquKiNkw"/>
    - Check linked references to see where the node has been discussed in meetings, logs, and other nodes. <roam uid="rsCUVEZGn"/>
    - For Results and Evidence, pay attention to the Source in the title and the Grounding Context section for methodological detail. <roam uid="rxcu3DrEs"/>
  - Linking to this graph <roam uid="sTxa7aNev" heading="3"/>
    - If you create a URL in the agentic chat UI (outside of roam), remember that the URL starts with `https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/`. The graph url is discourse-graphs; the graph MCP nickname is dg-team. <roam uid="8VfrwIAkz"/>
  - Formatting <roam uid="DLi8zMdfk" heading="3"/>
    - When writing in Roam, you can make use of colors, color underlines, and comments: <roam uid="UPWoTfgXC"/>
      - [[>]] [[!NOTE]] This is a basic note callout\nNotes are great for highlighting general information you want to draw attention to. <roam uid="GRXCvlZXR"/>
      - [[>]] [[!INFO]] Informational callout with an info icon\nUse these for additional context or background details. <roam uid="q9AGKeYbe"/>
      - [[>]] [[!SUMMARY]] A summary or abstract callout\nPerfect for executive summaries, TLDRs, or condensed overviews. <roam uid="-e0ZjrNmx"/>
      - [[>]] [[!TIP]] Helpful tip — try using callouts for emphasis!\nCombine callouts with **bold**, *italic*, and `code` formatting in both the title and body. <roam uid="QZj72rl96"/>
      - [[>]] [[!SUCCESS]] Operation completed successfully\nAll 47 tests passed. The deployment to staging is live. <roam uid="qnaPlXY2m"/>
      - [[>]] [[!QUESTION]] How do callouts work in Roam?\nThe first line after `[[!TYPE]]` is the title. Add body text on the next line with **Shift+Enter**. <roam uid="HQRN8neWv"/>
      - [[>]] [[!WARNING]] Be careful when editing shared pages\nOther users may be viewing or editing at the same time. <roam uid="tAydkxtXR"/>
      - [[>]] [[!FAILURE]] Build failed due to missing dependencies\nRun `npm install` and check that all peer dependencies are satisfied. <roam uid="gzwZx-squ"/>
      - [[>]] [[!DANGER]] Do NOT delete this page — critical data\nThis page contains production configuration values referenced by multiple systems. <roam uid="22V2wAMnL"/>
      - [[>]] [[!BUG]] Found a rendering issue on mobile viewports\nThe sidebar overlaps the main content when screen width is below 768px. <roam uid="JmKFXi5jT"/>
      - [[>]] [[!EXAMPLE]] Here's how you format a callout\nUse `[[>]] [[!TYPE]] Title` on the first line. Add body text with Shift+Enter. <roam uid="cLHhp8Dwj"/>
      - [[>]] [[!QUOTE]] "The best way to predict the future is to invent it."\n— Alan Kay, 1971 <roam uid="ACj_6GA26"/>
      - **Foldable Callouts** <roam uid="aUAi8OGtt"/>
        - Add `+` or `-` after the type (e.g. `[[!TIP]]+`) to make it foldable. `+` starts expanded, `-` starts collapsed. Click the header to toggle. <roam uid="zle_pzhMf"/>
